Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. name: The Editors at Broad + Liberty
subject: A landmark year for Broad + Liberty
body:
News + editorial | Broad + Liberty Weekly Reads | | | |
---
| | | Good morning, and welcome to _Broad + Liberty_ 's Wednesday Weekly Reads!

As always, to stay up to date on late-breaking stories and analysis, [subscribe to our daily email list](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=9f1dfa5518&e=b7b3eddce2) and get the best of _Broad + Liberty_ delivered straight to your inbox.
---
|
---
|
## **1. ****[Looking back at a landmark year for _Broad + Liberty_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=f22d21c10e&e=b7b3eddce2)**

_From the Editors _ It’s been a remarkable year at Broad +Liberty. We published over 900 original pieces covering wide-ranging topics from scandals in the Shapiro administration, county politics, education, culture and healthcare. Our investigative reporting by Todd Shepherd garnered state and national attention. The Pennsylvania News Media Association awarded Shepherd the “Best in Investigative Journalism” for his work exposing incompetence and poor management at the Delaware County prison. Nationally, the Atlantic cited Shepherd’s work in its lengthy piece on Governor Josh Shapiro. Broad + Liberty broke the news about a sexual harassment scandal involving one of Shapiro’s top aides back in 2023. Shepherd continues to uncover more concerning facts around the incident including deleted email accounts that run contrary to the state’s own policy. **Why It Matters.** From the founding of our republic, the health of our civic life has rested upon a simple but profound truth: a free and independent press is not merely a feature of democracy — it is one of its chief guarantors. As the only industry explicitly contemplated in the Constitution, the framers understood that liberty is not self-perpetuating; it must be renewed through informed citizens, accountable institutions, and a shared commitment to truth that transcends partisan preferences. As 2025 comes to a close, Broad + Liberty is excited for what 2026 has in store. Our team is ready to break the stories, report the news, and help our readers make sense of what is happening locally, across the state, and in the country. [_Continue Reading_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=7cff603d2c&e=b7b3eddce2)
---
|
---
|
# **2.**** [Give up the food, and other South Philly stories](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=cf21889521&e=b7b3eddce2)**

__ By Paul Davis Over the years that I’ve covered the crime beat in Philadelphia, I’ve gone out on many a ride along all over the city with Philadelphia police officers, but it seems that the most interesting and amusing occurrences all occurred in South Philadelphia where I grew up and continue to live. I recall some years ago while riding with a 3rd District patrol officer, we came upon a man who had chased away a would-be car break-in thief. From his house front window, the potential victim saw the young thief attempting to break into his car. The man ran out of his house with a baseball bat, and the thief took off so fast, he ran right out of his untied sneakers. The police officer took down the information for his report from the victim and the victim picked up the discarded sneakers and brought them into his house. Afterwards the cop had a good laugh as we sat in his patrol car. The cop told me that the sneakers the thief had left behind on the sidewalk were expensive — much more valuable than anything he could have stolen from the parked car. [_Continue Reading_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=a5686785aa&e=b7b3eddce2)
---
|
---
|
# **3. ****Lightning round**
* [_Richard Koenig: 2025 in review_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=375a0cf616&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Critics say Upper Darby Council violated Home Rule Charter_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=46e8490431&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Christine Flowers: In Britain, Boxing Day keeps holiday spirit alive_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=1f32803a50&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Thom Nickels: Too many cars_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=601bcf12b5&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Robert Daday: The price of Philadelphia’s courtroom jackpot_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=b08bd2dcbf&e=b7b3eddce2)[ __](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=4f17b25d05&e=b7b3eddce2)

---
|
---
|
# **4\. What we're reading. **
The Trump administration in 2025 faced the same challenge as Biden’s people did in 2024: an economy that looks good on paper but is not reflected in the national mood. The last quarter showed 4.3 percent annual growth in our economy — great news! — but people are still more likely to grouse about things than to feel satisfied. If you’re in the mood for a deep dive into the facts about this “vibecession” mindset, check out [_Scott Alexander’s essay_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=bb4dcd715c&e=b7b3eddce2). Facts don’t change vibes in politics, but they should give the reader something to think about.

body:
Help send a message to the extremists, the corporate executives, the billionaires, and the naysayers:

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2741%2E4032634%2E9oU3NW)
---
I’m going to make this very brief. Tonight we’ve got our last FEC fundraising deadline of the year. Before I ask you to pitch in to support our campaign, I want to explain exactly **why** this deadline is so important, and not just an abstract fundraising tactic. After tonight, our campaign’s fundraising numbers will be public. This will be one of the first assessments of our movement’s strength as we kick off the critical midterm election year. We’re going to be up against powerful special interests who are hoping to cling onto their power — and we’ve got big plans to ensure Democrats not only take back the House and Senate, but that we use our majorities to make aggressive, transformational changes in our country that benefit working people — even if billionaires and corporations disagree. The people who have the most to lose if we succeed — the far-right extremists who are destroying our democracy, the corporate executives siphoning resources from our government to enrich themselves, the billionaires who just can’t stand paying a little more in taxes, and the naysayers who believe that small, incremental changes are enough to meet this moment — they would love nothing more than to see our movement lose its steam. **After our fundraising report is published, we have a chance to show Trump, the GOP, and their billionaire enablers that you and thousands of others across the country are still in this fight — and that we are going to defeat them in 2026.** [**The amount of grassroots contributions we raise before tonight’s midnight deadline will send a powerful message about how much support we really have — and provide strong resources we need to power our fight in 2026. If, and only if, you’re able, will you please pitch in $28 or anything you can before midnight tonight?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3306?amount=28&t=8&akid=2741%2E4032634%2E9oU3NW) I don’t take your financial support lightly — and I’m grateful to have you in this fight no matter how much or how often you’re able to contribute. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

name: Mark Kelly
subject: My decision
body:
We’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. The President of the United States threatened my life, personally. I’ve got the entire executive branch bearing down on me right now.
Hey, Peter, it’s Mark Kelly.
Seven years ago, I was making a decision about whether I was going to run for the Senate.
I knew it would be a lot of work. A lot of time away from home. A lot of time away from family. I knew it wouldn’t be easy.
But after two years of Donald Trump and a Republican-held Senate doing just about everything he wanted, I knew I couldn’t sit on the sidelines. I had to do something.
So, I ran. And, somehow, we won. And then we had to turn around and run all over again to win a full term after that. But thanks to your support, we won that one, too.
I’m grateful every day that I get to wake up, walk out the door, and defend our people, our democracy, and our Constitution. It’s one of the greatest honors of my life. And I’ve never forgotten that I wouldn’t be here without your help.
We’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. The President of the United States threatened my life, personally. I’ve got the entire executive branch bearing down on me right now.
After everything you’ve already done for me, I shouldn’t have to ask you for more. But that’s what I need to do.
**[I’m asking you to split a donation between Wes Moore and me, and I hope you know that I wouldn’t be asking if this wasn’t important.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20251231-1.5lWK57&refcode=em-20251231-1&t=1&akid=1137%2E1086043%2EL4LYaF)**

Thank you.
Mark

Peter, This year, we’ve fought back against attacks at a scale and pace we’ve never seen before. New voter ID laws. The attempted theft of a state supreme court seat. A president openly demanding gerrymanders across the country to hold control of Congress. It’s brought us face-to-face with a hard truth: There are no reinforcements on the way. No miraculous rescue brigade is coming. **We are the cavalry.** And while this might seem daunting, it’s important to remember that this is how it has always been in the fight for a fairer, more equal America. The fight for equal protection under the law for people regardless of their race, gender, or sexual orientation didn’t happen because people sat on the sidelines. The fight for due process under the law didn’t happen because people wrung their hands. The fight for a truly representative democracy, where the will of the people prevails, didn’t happen because people crossed their fingers and hoped for the best. These fights have always been carried out by people like you: concerned Americans who are willing to roll up their sleeves and fight — because you know that rights and freedoms do not defend themselves. **Today is the last day of the year, Peter, and I’m sure your inbox is filled with worthy causes that need support.[I’m asking you today to make a donation to the NDRC to fight for fair maps — which we often like to say is the fight that makes all other fights possible.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/122325978/592273629/-1027206931?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_Dayof2_email_20251231-NDRC-Tier1-Dayof2_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20251231-NDRC-Tier1-Dayof2_&utm_campaign=Dayof2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ4YTBkZmJkLTUwZTYtZjAxMS04MTk1LTAwMGQzYTFkNThhYSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=gO1STkyuJFE2f6LBjrjGCVoDNwsQ0hHIJ1fJgJZrAzw=) ** Fight for fair maps so we can protect the rights of our immigrant neighbors. clean_body: Make a donation to the fight that makes all other fights possible. | Peter, This year, we’ve fought back against attacks at a scale and pace we’ve never seen before. New voter ID laws. The attempted theft of a state supreme court seat. A president openly demanding gerrymanders across the country to hold control of Congress. It’s brought us face-to-face with a hard truth: There are no reinforcements on the way. No miraculous rescue brigade is coming. We are the cavalry. And while this might seem daunting, it’s important to remember that this is how it has always been in the fight for a fairer, more equal America. The fight for equal protection under the law for people regardless of their race, gender, or sexual orientation didn’t happen because people sat on the sidelines. The fight for due process under the law didn’t happen because people wrung their hands. The fight for a truly representative democracy, where the will of the people prevails, didn’t happen because people crossed their fingers and hoped for the best. These fights have always been carried out by people like you: concerned Americans who are willing to roll up their sleeves and fight — because you know that rights and freedoms do not defend themselves. subject: 2025 Annual Report
body:
This year brought a new chapter for Greater Georgia with the same mission and spirit
| | | | |
---
|
Friends,
2025 has been an exciting year of change for Greater Georgia.
In 2021, Greater Georgia was founded by former U.S. Senator Kelly Loeffler with a mission to build a year-round conservative operation focused on registration, voter education and mobilization, and election integrity.
Four years later, after conservatives saw the fruits of their labor in 2024, Senator Loeffler accepted a new role in President Trump's administration.
With that transition, Greater Georgia entered a new chapter with the same mission.
In 2025, Greater Georgia continued this work by:

* Launching a six-figure campaign and successfully registering 17,309 new conservative voters

* Hosting a statewide tour across Georgia to educate voter's about state legislation

* Mobilizing 84,000 low-propensity voters in the November 2025 elections

* Serving as Election Integrity first responders when Chatham County lost absentee ballots in the mail

We hope you enjoy our full year-end report, sharing these highlights and much more.
---

body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2393%2E135344%2Etj6Pgw)

**Let's recap where we're at ... and then I am going to ask you to make a contribution to help me fight back.**
Last month, shortly before Thanksgiving, President Trump threatened me and a number of other service and veteran lawmakers with arrest, trial ...
...because he didn't agree with a video we put out.
His response unleashed a series of very real consequences. Immediately after Trump's initial response, I received a tidal wave of death threats, and was placed under 24 hour security protection.
I wish I could say that was the end ... but it was not.
Shortly after, the FBI's Counterterrorism Division appeared to open an inquiry into me in response to the video and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has threatened my friend, Senator Mark Kelly, with court-martial.
The truth is, President Trump believes in weaponizing the federal government against his perceived enemies and does not believe laws apply to him or his Cabinet. He uses legal harassment as an intimidation tactic to scare people out of speaking up. He’s done it to law firms, universities, private sector companies, and private individuals.
Now he is trying it on me.
It won't work.
I swore an oath to the Constitution, many times, most recently less than a year ago as a United States Senator.
An oath to the Constitution -- not to any one man, not to any one president.
I abide by that oath.
I have always worked to be upfront and honest in these emails. These threats from the FBI mean we've had to start thinking through a legal defense strategy because we have no idea where President Trump and his Justice Department will end up taking this inquiry.
Today is New Year's Eve -- it's an FEC fundraising deadline but also a natural break point where we'll take stock of the resources we have to fight back when it ends.
So while I know your inbox is flooded with requests from campaigns and organizations asking for your donations, I had hoped explaining what your support would go toward for me would help you consider tossing a few bucks my way before midnight.
Here's a link:

My team and I are up against a public filing deadline tonight at midnight. It’s the last public report of the year. Once it’s filed, everyone, including our opponents, will be watching to see exactly where we stand, and how strong we are, entering this critical election year.

_**EXHIBIT 1 - JOINT FUNDRAISING NOTICE **_

Team Nunn ("JFC") is a joint fundraising committee composed of Iowans for Zach Nunn ("Campaign"), Call to Service PAC ("LPAC") and NRCC (each, a "Committee," and, collectively, the "Committees"). Any contribution to the JFC permissible under the Federal Election Campaign Act, as amended ("FECA"), from contributors who have not exceeded their applicable federal contribution limits, shall be allocated among the Committees pursuant to FECA and the formula set forth in this Notice.

_**Contributions Made by an Individual or Federal Non-Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Individuals or federal non-multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $322,100. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $7,000, designating up to $3,500 to the primary election and up to $3,500 to the general election, provided such limits apply.
2\. LPAC shall receive any contribution not exceeding $5,000 annually.
3\. NRCC shall receive for its general account any contribution not exceeding $44,300 annually.
4\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $132,900 for its Building Fund, provided such limits apply.
5\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $132,900 for its Legal Proceedings Fund, provided such limits apply.

_**Contributions Made by a Federal Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $120,000. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $10,000, designating up to $5,000 to the primary election and up to $5,000 to the general election, provided such limits apply.
2\. LPAC shall receive any contribution not exceeding $5,000 annually.
3 .NRCC shall receive for its general account any contribution not exceeding $15,000 annually.
4\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $45,000 for its Building Fund, provided such limits apply.
5 .NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $45,000 for its Legal Proceedings Fund, provided such limits apply.

Contributions to Team Nunn, or to any participating Committee individually, are not deductible as charitable donations for federal income tax purposes. Contributions from corporations, labor organizations, national banks, federal government contractors, foreign nationals without green cards, and other federally impermissible sources are prohibited. The contributor's signature designates his or her contribution to the elections described above. Contributions that exceed a donor's contribution limit to a participating Committee shall be reallocated to the remaining Committees according to this allocation formula to the extent permitted by FECA. Any contributor may designate his or her contribution to a specific participant Committee to the extent permitted by FECA. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, mailing address, occupation, and name of employer of each individual whose aggregate contributions exceed $200 in an election cycle or calendar year, as applicable.

Team Nunn ("JFC") is a joint fundraising committee composed of Iowans for Zach Nunn ("Campaign"), Call to Service PAC ("LPAC") and NRCC (each, a "Committee," and, collectively, the "Committees"). Any contribution to the JFC permissible under the Federal Election Campaign Act, as amended ("FECA"), from contributors who have not exceeded their applicable federal contribution limits, shall be allocated among the Committees pursuant to FECA and the formula set forth in this Notice.

_**Contributions Made by an Individual or Federal Non-Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Individuals or federal non-multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $322,100. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $7,000, designating up to $3,500 to the primary election and up to $3,500 to the general election, provided such limits apply.
2\. LPAC shall receive any contribution not exceeding $5,000 annually.
3\. NRCC shall receive for its general account any contribution not exceeding $44,300 annually.
4\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $132,900 for its Building Fund, provided such limits apply.
5\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $132,900 for its Legal Proceedings Fund, provided such limits apply.

_**Contributions Made by a Federal Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $120,000. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $10,000, designating up to $5,000 to the primary election and up to $5,000 to the general election, provided such limits apply.
2\. LPAC shall receive any contribution not exceeding $5,000 annually.
3 .NRCC shall receive for its general account any contribution not exceeding $15,000 annually.
4\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $45,000 for its Building Fund, provided such limits apply.
5 .NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $45,000 for its Legal Proceedings Fund, provided such limits apply.

Contributions to Team Nunn, or to any participating Committee individually, are not deductible as charitable donations for federal income tax purposes. Contributions from corporations, labor organizations, national banks, federal government contractors, foreign nationals without green cards, and other federally impermissible sources are prohibited. The contributor's signature designates his or her contribution to the elections described above. Contributions that exceed a donor's contribution limit to a participating Committee shall be reallocated to the remaining Committees according to this allocation formula to the extent permitted by FECA. Any contributor may designate his or her contribution to a specific participant Committee to the extent permitted by FECA. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, mailing address, occupation, and name of employer of each individual whose aggregate contributions exceed $200 in an election cycle or calendar year, as applicable.

Good morning, friend! ☀️
I'm an early riser, always have been. If the sun's up, I'm up, ready to dive into my day. On this final day of 2025, I'm enjoying a slower morning than usual, reflecting on the year we've had over a strong cup of coffee, and I thought I'd send you a quick note.
I know this has been a challenging year for so many of us. The Trump administration's economic "policies," attacks on Medicaid and SNAP benefits, and dangerous agenda have put so many families in an incredibly tough spot.
**That's one of the many reasons I was inspired to launch this campaign to fight for a better, more affordable future for all New Mexican families.**
I'm so proud of everything we've accomplished since then, from the fruitful conversations I've had with people in every county across the state, to the thousands of grassroots donors who have chipped in to power our movement.
**[But with everything that's at stake next year, for the future of New Mexico, and with Republicans already gearing up to try and buy this governor seat, I'm asking you to please make donation to my campaign before midnight tonight. Our $50,000 year-end goal is ambitious, but with your help, I know we can get there and give this team the best chance of winning — and delivering for New Mexicans — in 2026.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/3595?t=3&akid=6589%2E400544%2Eu2VPqr)**
Thank you so much for being a part of my team — and happy new year, friend!
💛 Deb

Minnesota just got caught in what investigators are calling [one of the largest welfare fraud schemes in American history](https://substack.com/redirect/23b7606f-35f1-4919-a168-154ae7db4c24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Billions of dollars in childcare subsidies stolen by foreigners while hardworking American families struggle to make ends meet.
But this isn't just happening in Minnesota.
This fraud is rampant across the country wherever childcare subsidies lack proper oversight, and Idaho has the exact same structural weaknesses in our system that allowed billions to walk out the door in other states. We're a target, and I refuse to sit around and wait to become the next cautionary tale.
That's why I just sent a letter to the Idaho Department of Health and Human Services requesting an immediate pause on $14 million in new childcare appropriations until we can install proper fraud prevention measures.
I voted against Senate Bill 1206 during the 2025 session because it appropriated over $14 million in new childcare subsidies without adequate fraud prevention safeguards in place. The bill dumps money into building childcare supply through contracted spots, grants, and subgrants...
_**But it does nothing to ensure that money actually reaches legitimate providers serving real Idaho families.**_
Minnesota's billion-dollar disaster proves exactly why proper safeguards matter before you start writing checks. This isn't about stopping support for working families who need quality childcare, because those families deserve better than a system riddled with fraud that drives up costs and reduces access to legitimate providers.
[| | | | | Collin Rugg
---
@CollinRugg
NEW: Minnesota man absolutely loses his mind during Nick Shirley's investigation into fraud, accuses him of wanting the Somali community in concentration camps. Shirley was seen keeping his cool as the man grew increasingly unhinged. Man: You are attacking the Somali
| 6:54 PM * Dec 30, 2025 * 1.45M Views4.74K Replies * 7.71K Reposts * 37K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/f0b7164b-a529-443b-b86c-41d771d3d835?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The American worker gets up every day, pays their taxes, and expects their government to be a responsible steward of those hard-earned dollars.
This is what being America First is all about: putting Americans first (this shouldn't even be controversial). But when fraudsters exploit weak oversight to steal millions or billions, it's the working families who pay the price twice: once through their taxes and again when they can't find affordable childcare because scammers have crowded out legitimate providers.
Good news though!
We have two former Idahoans now serving at the federal level who understand our systems inside and out. Former IDHW Director Alex Adams serves as Assistant Secretary for the Administration of Children and Families, and former Representative Wendy Horman will soon lead the Office of Child Care. We have an opportunity to get this right before we have a problem, and that's exactly what we're going to do.
Along with Representative Josh Tanner, I've requested that IDHW develop comprehensive fraud prevention measures, review past disbursements for potential fraud, and brief the Legislature on their plan before moving forward. We've asked for a response by January 10th.
Working families deserve a childcare system they can trust. Taxpayers deserve accountability. We're going to deliver both.

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Talarico for Texas
body:
#
Peter —
You probably know what I am about to ask. I know I’ve asked a number of times, so before I ask for your financial support today, I think you deserve an explanation.
Before I was a candidate for U.S. Senate, like you, I read a lot of emails from candidates about how important these FEC deadlines were. Well, I can say first-hand the stakes and pressure you feel as a candidate are very real.
These deadlines are important as a matter of transparency. When we report our numbers to the Federal Election Commission, the public will see exactly who is funding our campaign — and our opponents.
I’m proud to show the world that this is a true grassroots campaign. We’re funded by the people. We’re the only campaign in this race that has never taken a dime of corporate PAC money.
But that makes our task that much harder. They can call one corporate PAC to give them $10,000. With our average donation around $30, it takes over 300 people giving to match that. That's why asks like this one are so important:
**[Please, if you can, make a contribution today. It’s critical that we have as many donations as possible before tonight’s FEC deadline. Each one is a powerful show of force for our movement.](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-launch.bF5RK3&refcode=em251231-1-ak&t=1&akid=362%2E1347274%2E2aMFZd)**
The numbers we report are also analyzed by the media and our opponents. They’ll be judging if our movement has what it takes to beat the billionaire mega-donors and their puppet politicians.
In this new and more expensive race we face, a weak report means political pundits and the corporate media will write us off before Texans even get a chance to make their voice heard.
We can’t let that happen.
We set a goal for our fundraising that will ensure that does not happen — one that can show we have sustained our momentum and only grown stronger. But truthfully, we still have some ground to make up to get there.
I’m hoping you can help us send a message loud and clear that the people have our back. We won’t be bullied by the attack ads they’ve already run against me or their billionaire mega-donors.
**[That’s why I’m humbly asking you to please contribute $5 or whatever you can to our campaign today. I cannot do this alone.](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-launch.bF5RK3&refcode=em251231-1-ak&t=2&akid=362%2E1347274%2E2aMFZd)**

# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240572%2E444211%2EvNF_jK)
Texas is at a crossroads. Voting rights are under attack. Working families are under attack. Our communities are under attack.
But Powered by People refuses to sit on the sidelines. We organize. We register voters. We mobilize communities to fight for the leaders and representation we deserve.
Republicans will stop at nothing to steal and consolidate power. From pushing gerrymandered maps to threatening Democrats who stand up for what’s right, they aren’t slowing down.
_But neither are we._
Every volunteer signed up, new voter registered, community event hosted, and conversation held in neighborhoods across Texas is about giving people the tools to fight back — not letting politicians decide their lives and futures for them.
But here’s the truth: we can’t do it without you. Tonight is the last chance to chip in ahead of the new year. | | , As 2025 comes to a close, I want to take a moment to reflect on what we’ve built together and what it will take to win in 2026. Earlier this year, I entered the race for Texas Attorney General because I believe this office should serve the people, not political ambition or cruelty. Since then, we’ve been hard at work. I’ve traveled Texas corner to corner, showing up at **more than 100 events** across cities, towns, and counties. I’ve listened to voters in living rooms, union halls, college campuses, and community meetings. I’ve debated one of my opponents, answered tough questions, and stood shoulder to shoulder with Texans on **No Kings Day** to affirm a simple truth: no one is above the law. What I’ve heard everywhere is consistent. Texans are tired of chaos. They want honesty, competence, and leadership that puts people first. **That’s what this campaign is about.** Now we turn the page to 2026, the year Texans choose a new Attorney General. Winning will take early organizing, strong communication, statewide visibility, and the resources to compete all the way through March. **That’s why****December 31 matters**. What we raise before the end of the year is a meaningful signal of momentum to everyone watching this race—supporters, volunteers, endorsers, and voters. It also directly fuels the work ahead, from outreach and organizing to getting our message in front of Texans who haven’t heard it yet. [**If you believe in what we’ve built in 2025 and want to help carry it forward into a winning 2026, I’m asking you to make a year-end contribution today.**](https://jaworskifortexas.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2e1f50319ad85f5f9e5c11ac9&id=61a3f3d6a8&e=5d8d80652b) Together, we’ve laid the foundation. Now let’s finish the job. Onward!

**

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Grateful for all your support so far and asking for your help again
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Heartland Patriots (LucasKunce
body:
Couldn’t do this without you.
Hi Peter — _I want to say thank you._
I know you’re probably tired of seeing all my requests for your donation coming through your inbox (I wish I didn’t have to send them so often, either). But in a race this close, every dollar counts. Emails like this one are our best way of earning your financial investment.
Although I will have to **[ask for your support](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/98692?refcode=em20251231-9856&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=9856%2E614464%2EfbN5Go)** today as well — we have a huge end-of-quarter filing deadline tonight, after all — **my first priority today is to make sure you know how truly grateful I am.**
The outpouring of support our campaign has received so far has surpassed all my hopes. We are in a strong position in this toss-up race, and that’s all because of the momentum we’re building together.
You know, when I ran for public office the very first time in Nash County, NC, there were a lot of folks who had my back. Nash County is where I grew up. People there knew me and trusted me to do right by them. Without their help, I never could have won that first election.
**The stakes are even higher now, and I’m humbled to say that more and more of you are putting your faith and trust in us every day. You are the reason that I know that we can win the most competitive U.S. Senate race of 2026.**
In a race of national importance like this one, I don’t get as many chances to thank enough supporters personally, so it’s important to me to share my appreciation now. _Thank you._
Peter, if you’ve been thinking about making a donation to our campaign, it would mean a lot if you could do so right now. We set a big goal for this filing deadline — a million dollars. That’s what we need to raise to take on my far-right opponent, who has dark-money groups and PACs lined up and ready to spend _hundreds of millions_ against me. And after this deadline, we’ll need to file a public report, so falling short really isn’t an option. We can’t give the GOP that kind of opportunity to seize the momentum.
**[Please, split anything that fits in your budget between our campaign and Heartland Patriots. Your investment in our campaign is what will make it possible for us to succeed.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/98692?refcode=em20251231-9856&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=9856%2E614464%2EfbN5Go)**

body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]

The year 2025 has brought so many challenges. And for those of us who campaigned for different outcomes in 2024, it was worse than we imagined it could be.
We have seen the systematic and strategic dismantling of programs not only that people rely on but that define who we are and what we value. Supporting one another in times of need. Staying informed and engaged. Sharing democracy and democratic values with the world.
As House Republicans and President Trump attacked Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security, Nutrition Assistance, National Public Radio; dismantled the National Institutes of Health, the Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Education, the Department of State, USAID, and more, they also attacked our friends and neighbors here in TX07 and across the country–seeking to divide Americans and dismantling the American Dream.
It has been a hard year. But today marks its end. And tomorrow, a new year begins. A year that brings with it the possibility for change. Real change.
Now, we can’t change everything overnight. But winning the mid-term elections is a critical first step. By taking back the House, we can put a check on this reckless administration. We can stop the enabling. We can restore the checks and balances our government needs and Americans rely on.
And we can do it together.
We are all working as hard as ever to do our part—from winning our election in TX07 to supporting candidates on the ballot in Texas and in competitive races around the country.
To do that, we need to meet the goals we set for ourselves—including our final quarterly fundraising goal of the year.
DONATE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe251231?refcode=lpfe251231]
Your response to these deadlines and your generous contributions are so meaningful. I’m so grateful for this team and all you’ve done this year to set us up for success in 2026. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe251231?refcode=lpfe251231]
In a time of unprecedented challenges at home and across the country, your engagement reminds us why we do this work, who we’re fighting for, and how much we can accomplish when we do it together. I look forward to doing this work with you in 2026. And celebrating our successful efforts next November!
Together we can do anything,

None of this would have been possible without you.

[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/3536?t=7&akid=255%2E124072%2EAUQZA6) Good morning, Peter — On this last day of 2025, I am reflecting on all the changes this year has brought. **[I’d like to share some thoughts with you, but first I need to ask you to invest in our campaign for the U.S. Senate by donating before midnight. When the year ends, we’ll need to file a public financial report, and it’s important that we show everyone our momentum remains strong.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/3536?t=8&akid=255%2E124072%2EAUQZA6)** **It started off with the end of my time as Governor.** All I’ve ever wanted to do was give back to the state that I love so much. Having the opportunity to serve as Governor for eight years meant more to me than I can say — and we got a lot done. We expanded Medicaid to more than 700,000 people and created jobs by investing in building a clean energy economy. We invested in early learning and childcare to give kids the strong start they deserve and established North Carolina as the #1 state for business three of the last four years. I left office with a deep gratitude for having this chance to serve and for all those whose help made it possible. **I spent the first few months of 2025 thinking hard about what might come next.** It kept nagging at me that I needed to do something more to make a difference. And when I thought about this Senate seat, I thought about how the same kinds of people-first policies that we put forth here in NC could help families across the country. And I saw how important this seat was not only for our state, but for the nation as a whole. **So I spent some time talking with my family about it and praying on it, and then I decided. I would run for office yet again, and because I know my country needs me.** Peter, the enthusiasm and encouragement we received when we started out on this campaign was like nothing I could have imagined. I’m grateful for everyone who has stepped up with a donation, shared news of our campaign online, or reached out with support. Our people-centered movement has grown even more in the months since then. **But it hasn’t all been easy. The right-wing GOP is united against us — they see our campaign as the top threat to their one-party hold on power. President Trump handpicked my opponent, and Trump has even attacked me personally.** I am clear-eyed about what’s ahead: This is going to be the most difficult race I’ve ever run. We expect it to become the most expensive Senate race in history due to the GOP’s mega-donors and super PACs spending against us. I know I can’t take them on alone. **[Tonight is our final end-of-quarter deadline of 2025. Tomorrow, our election year begins. I am ready for the fight ahead, but I can only win it with your help. clean_body: I’ve been thinking a lot about what Wisconsin has accomplished — and what’s still at stake. | | | | Happy New Year’s Eve, Derek! As we get ready to ring in a new year, I’ve been thinking a lot about what Wisconsin has accomplished — and what’s still at stake. Since I’ve been governor, we’ve made real progress putting people first, fixing the damn roads, making sure every Wisconsin gets fed, ensuring schools are well funded and so much more. But take it from me: this fight is just getting started. With 2026 on the horizon, Republicans are already gearing up to ensure whoever their nominee is has the resources they need to take our state backwards. Ensuring that doesn’t happen is why we have the battleground program. We need to raise $25,000 into the battleground program by midnight. Battleground Wisconsin ensures that whomever Wisconsin Democrats nominate to run for Governor will have a campaign in waiting ready to fight back and win. Team,

first time in decades, expand civil rights, and pass common-sense gun
laws.

must-win for Democrats in 2026. If we want to put a stop to Trump and his

subject: A note on 2025:
body:
---
Derek, Our end-of-quarter fundraising deadline is coming up at midnight, and in a minute, I’m going to [**personally ask for your support.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-december-2025?amount=7&refcode=em_20251231_5591_fr&refcode2=5591_22930333_XPCkMu&akid=5591%2E22930333%2EXPCkMu) Trust me, these deadlines really matter. Our team sets quarterly goals that allow us to invest in winning races up and down the ballot. And when you believe that every election matters — like I do — then hitting our goals makes all the difference. As we head into 2026, our spending decisions are more important than ever. Derek, the midterms are here, and to stop Trump, we can’t leave anything to chance. We’ve seen over and over again this year that when Democrats invest, and when we compete everywhere, we can win anywhere. We’ve won races all over the country — from Mississippi to Wisconsin to Arizona and beyond. We’ve flipped seats in places that haven’t had a Democratic leader in decades. We can’t afford to lose momentum now. As you can imagine, we’ve put in a lot of work this year. And it takes serious resources to build strong volunteer bases, reach voters, and ensure people have a plan to show up on Election Day. But thanks to people like you, we’ve been on the march in 2025. Now, it’s time to sprint. So I’m reaching out to ask you to make a $7 contribution to the DNC before midnight. $7 to ensure we can continue to invest in _every single_ Democratic state party. $7 to help us scale up our voter outreach well before Election Day. $7 to help win back Congress and prevent another two years of Trump with no guardrails. subject: My Four Best Pieces of 2025
body:
As this year ends, and AI slop is everywhere, I've been feeling very grateful that I have the freedom to think and write. I wanted to share four pieces I wrote this year that I'm especially proud of. Each one, in its own way, grapples with power, who holds it, how it hides, and what it does to human experience. | | | As this year ends, and AI slop is everywhere, I've been feeling very grateful that I have the freedom to think and write. I wanted to share four pieces I wrote this year that I'm especially proud of. Each one, in its own way, grapples with power, who holds it, how it hides, and what it does to human experience.If you're looking for something to read during the quieter days ahead, I hope one (or more) of these might be worth your time:**1\. When It Comes to Understanding the Dangers Posed by Big Tech, We 're Lost in the Cloud**
I wrote about how "the cloud" and AI are treated as abstract and inevitable, when in fact they are physical systems and deeply political systems, controlled by a handful of corporations with enormous influence over our economy, speech, and our future.
https://www.thenation.com/article/society/ai-cloud-big-tech-dangers/**2\. New York City Has the Power to Bring Down Grocery Prices. All Cities Do.**
As some of you know, I'm on Mamdani's legal transition team. But before that happened, I wrote for the New York Times making the case for municipal power at a moment when many people are told there's nothing to be done about rising food prices. Cities have more leverage than we're led to believe--I'm hopeful that Mamdani is going to use many of these tools.
https://www.nytimes.com/2025/07/21/opinion/nyc-grocery-prices.html**3\. How a New Media Oligarchy Fuels Corruption and Concentrated Power**
The Trump scandals can be overwhelming, but as I argue in this piece, his corruption is enabled by media consolidation. We tend to think of antitrust and corruption in separate buckets, but the Jimmy Kimmel scandal shows how concentrated control over information becomes the ground on which corruption thrives.
https://www.thenation.com/article/culture/media-oligarchy-trump-corruption/**4\. Selling a Defective Dream**
This is the one I'm most proud of- I love writing for the New York Review of Books- its in part a review essay of the great new book on ponzi schemes, _Little Bosses Everywhere,_ and in part a reflection on how the categories of worker and consumer are getting increasingly blurred, and how that enables mass scamming in a heartbreaking way.
https://www.nybooks.com/articles/2025/12/04/selling-a-defective-dream-little-bosses-everywhere-bridget-read/I'm grateful to everyone who reads, shares, argues back, and keeps these conversations alive. Writing is hard, but a privilege, and I don't take that for granted.Wishing you rest, joy, and moments of democracy in the year ahead.With gratitude,
Zephyr[Support this newsletter. ](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/f76615f4?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21)(Also supergrateful that Tim Wu is now also joining me in this newsletter! Antimonopolists, unite!)

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/122353706/592355510/2105508926?refcode=ea.e3a90b19-61e6-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&ms=ea.e3a90b19-61e6-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImUzYTkwYjE5LTYxZTYtZjAxMS04MTk1LTAwMGQzYTFkNThhYSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=g8gj20rB8l-42c7rZDmm7vff9FKxt1-wgKxx9fTqrsI=) I’ve been thinking a lot about New Year’s resolutions, and I wanted to share mine: to do everything in my power to ensure we can elect brave, bold climate champions and flip the *flipping* House in 2026. **[If that sounds like the kind of year you want to be part of, I’m humbly asking you to chip in a few dollars before our final fundraising deadline of 2025 so we can start the new year strong.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/122353715/592355517/2105508926?refcode=ea.e3a90b19-61e6-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&ms=ea.e3a90b19-61e6-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImUzYTkwYjE5LTYxZTYtZjAxMS04MTk1LTAwMGQzYTFkNThhYSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=g8gj20rB8l-42c7rZDmm7vff9FKxt1-wgKxx9fTqrsI=)** For decades, we've been told we have time. That we can deal with the climate crisis in four years, after the next election, or when the right leader comes along. But that's just not true anymore. Our planet doesn't have four more years. Our frontline communities don’t have four years. The fight is happening right now, and every moment matters. As you read this, Donald Trump is consolidating power at record speed, dismantling environmental protections, attacking freedom of speech and expression, and hollowing out the very institutions meant to protect us. At the same time, billionaires like Elon Musk are pouring money into Republican campaigns to lock in control of Congress and silence opposition. They're betting we'll get tired. They're counting on us to stay quiet. They’re hoping we’ll give up. **But I’ve lived long enough to recognize this playbook — and to know we win when we rise up together. Fox 7 Austin: New Postal Service guidance on postmarks could affect ballot, tax deadlines [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=123125_1&amount=25]
The day you mail something may no longer count as the actual mailing date, Team.
Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office.
USPS has now reversed that practice. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility, not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over.
What does this mean? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. Derek, I want to wish you a very happy New Year! I think we’re all excited to be turning the page to what may be a brighter year ahead.
For far too many, this year hasn’t been an easy one. There is much turmoil here in our country and all around the world, and I know that we all endure our own personal hardships day in and day out.
You’ve heard me say this before — as I learned from my mom, Kathy — if you want to be right, be a pessimist; if you want to do right, be an optimist. So I remain, as ever, an optimist about what we can do together.
That doesn’t mean I don’t feel frustrated, disappointed, and dismayed at so much of what’s going on, and what this Administration has done over the past 11 months. But I wake up every morning determined to do whatever I can to make things better for my constituents and everyone who is counting on their leaders to fight for them. I believe that it is indeed possible to get things done and create a brighter future.
As we count down to the end of 2025 and the start of a brand new year — one with major opportunities to make changes! — I want to thank you from the bottom of my heart for everything you’ve done to support this work.
2026 will be full of more hard work, both in pushing back on the challenges created by a reckless President, and in fighting to elect and re-elect so many of our great Democrats who will be on the ballot next November.
I’m ready for it — and if you’re able to pitch in any amount in these final hours before our last FEC deadline of the year, it would mean so much to me. Every donation goes directly to our work for Democratic victories in 2026! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2025]

body:
Dear Peter,
Today is the last day we have to reach our $75,000 end-of-year fundraising goal before midnight’s deadline. We still have a little ways to go, so I wanted to write to you directly.
If you’re ready to help us reach our goal, can you chip in right now? I had my team make this custom link for you: **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_kp_20251231_1_ak?personal=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20251231_1_ak.qkRQ2R&refcode=em20251231-40636&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=40636%2E3422442%2EqIZRrJ)**
Here’s why reaching this goal matters so much:
The end of the month is a major filing deadline for California gubernatorial campaigns. Every candidate—including my opponents—has to tell the world exactly how much money they’ve raised.
I’ve been through deadlines like this before, so I can tell you first hand that everyone will be watching our numbers extremely closely. If we look weak, national Republicans could look to give more support to the GOP candidates who have been leading the polls. That could box Democrats out of the general election altogether!
We can’t afford for that to happen—not with our California values at stake. But I’m not worried because this grassroots team has had my back when I’ve needed it the most, and I’m counting on it to step up again today.
Peter, can you donate $5 or more to our campaign today to help us reach our $75,000 goal and show that this movement isn’t backing down? Chip in at this link: **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_kp_20251231_1_ak?personal=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20251231_1_ak.qkRQ2R&refcode=em20251231-40636&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=40636%2E3422442%2EqIZRrJ)**
Thank you so much for being a supporter and taking the time to read this email.
Best,
—Katie

Minneapolis is under full-scale attack right now from the far-right.
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2018%2E791427%2EbgLSxq)

Friend — it’s New Year’s Eve. We have a huge FEC deadline tonight. We wish we didn’t have to talk about this.
But it’s too important.
So let’s be honest: **If Republicans tried to expel Ilhan from Congress, it would be for nothing other than partisan, racist spite.**
You’re reading this email because you know Ilhan. You see her fight every day for the most vulnerable among us. You see her commitment to fairness, affordability, democracy, and her community.
But Minneapolis is under full-scale attack right now from the far-right. They have zeroed in on Ilhan and Somali-Americans because they need a new topic to rile people up and get mileage out of on Fox News.
But to take this even further, and attempt to expel Ilhan on no real basis at all, would be starkly authoritarian and set a dangerous precedent for the future. That’s why we have to be ready for anything that comes next.
Thankfully we have an opportunity with tonight’s FEC deadline to send a message to anyone who wants to mess with Ilhan that she has a huge team by her side.
We won’t be intimidated. We won’t fall for anti-immigrant scapegoating.
[**Please, chip in whatever you can afford and stand against these GOP attacks. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud. In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson. In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. Through live events, educational experiences, historical showcases, and local collaborations, the US 250 Tour brings communities
together from coast to coast to celebrate the people, stories, and values that define our nation.

This is an opportunity to share the remarkable story of America, honor our heroes, and celebrate the innovation, creativity, and
resilience of the American people. From our farmers and ranchers to the Space Coast and the entertainment industry, everyone will
have an opportunity to participate in this historic tour.

At each stop, visitors will be welcomed to Freedom Village, a traveling patriotic festival hosting stages for national and local
performers, family-focused activities, Liberty Kids America, interactive educational exhibits, immersive AI-driven history
experiences, and State Heritage Pavilions. Evenings will conclude with The Great American JourneyTM, a multimedia stage production
that merges historical reenactments with live, original music.

Families will also be invited to participate in Liberty TripsTM, an engaging adventure exploring historical sites in each state,
guided by historians, historic reenactors, special guests, celebrities, and the tour’s mascot, Liberty the Beagle.

clean_body: The US 250 Freedom Tour, officially Kicks off in Mesquite, Nevada, January 9th -11th. If you are having trouble viewing this email click here to view in your browser. [] [] [] MOMS FOR AMERICA LAUNCHES HISTORIC YEAR-LONG CELEBRATION WITH US 250 TOUR! I am very excited to announce, after months of collaborating with the White House 250 Taskforce, the President has officially announced Freedom 250 – a collaboration of public and private partnerships. The Freedom 250 Network includes federal, state, and local governments, corporations, civic organizations, cultural and educational institutions, faith-based and philanthropic partners – giving every American, and friends of America, an opportunity to celebrate this historic milestone. Everyone can sign up at Freedom250.org [] to learn more. You can see the president’s official announcement here: [] [] Moms for America is excited to be a part of this historic celebration as a Founding Member of the Freedom 250 network and the collaborative opportunities this network provides to unite the American people around this historic celebration. As part of this year-long celebration, I am thrilled to announce the official launch of the US 250 Freedom Tour Produced in partnership with Moms for America, Inc., and GFM Productions Inspired by the post-World War II Friendship and Merci Trains [], the US 250 Freedom Tour sparks a sense of gratitude and ignites a revival of the American Spirit through music, storytelling, education, and family-centered activities. Through live events, educational experiences, historical showcases, and local collaborations, the US 250 Tour brings communities together from coast to coast to celebrate the people, stories, and values that define our nation. This is an opportunity to share the remarkable story of America, honor our heroes, and celebrate the innovation, creativity, and resilience of the American people. From our farmers and ranchers to the Space Coast and the entertainment industry, everyone will have an opportunity to participate in this historic tour. At each stop, visitors will be welcomed to Freedom Village, a traveling patriotic festival hosting stages for national and local performers, family-focused activities, Liberty Kids America, interactive educational exhibits, immersive AI-driven history experiences, and State Heritage Pavilions. Evenings will conclude with The Great American JourneyTM, a multimedia stage production that merges historical reenactments with live, original music. Families will also be invited to participate in Liberty TripsTM, an engaging adventure exploring historical sites in each state, guided by historians, historic reenactors, special guests, celebrities, and the tour’s mascot, Liberty the Beagle. [] [] [] The US 250 Freedom Tour, officially Kicks off in Mesquite, Nevada, January 9th -11th. The year-long tour will bring American history to life through community, culture, and patriotism while uniting citizens across the country in a shared celebration of American freedom, innovation, faith, family, and the American dream. If you would like to be part of the US 250 Tour as a volunteer, sponsor, or just want to stay in the loop visit: US250Tour.com [] We are looking for storytellers, historic reenactors, and volunteers to help with Liberty Kids America for the Freedom Village. We also need help with some of our curriculum and project development. Please contact Moms for America if you would like to volunteer or have projects, concepts, or connections you would like us to consider. Lots of photos are loading right now, so let me use the next few moments to quickly say:
1. It's been a wonderful, purposeful year as your AG.

2. We won _a lot_ of big cases, like protecting SNAP funding for 600,000 kids in our state, $165 million for public education, $220 million from FEMA, $230 million in health care funding, $150 million from Purdue Pharma to fight the fentanyl epidemic, and dozens more solid wins for our state.

3. We opened up a major front in the war against robocalls.

4. We've focused heavily on public safety, working with law enforcement on fentanyl, Helene recovery, and going after violent offenders. Our law enforcement partners have been outstanding.

5. Inside NCDOJ, our team has performed at a very high level. You may never meet most of them, but I see their work every day, and they're exceptionally good at defending you from a wide range of threats.

6. On a personal note, I'm really proud of our family. Marisa, Haden, Owen, and Avery did great this year, despite all the stress and change that comes with a new job like this.

Now, here's looking back at the last 12 months:

Your support really matters. I believe in keeping people informed about the work we're doing, even when it's not an election year.
That's why I do these emails, but for folks who aren't subscribed, that's also why I created the Lighthouse Fund - to reach folks who otherwise wouldn't hear about any of this.
If you're able to make a contribution before the end of the year, I'd really appreciate it. Jeff

body:
https://kellyforcongress.org [https://kellyforcongress.org]
Hi Peter,
Kelly Morrison here — Happy New Year’s Eve! As we bid farewell to a tumultuous 2025, I wanted to take a moment to reflect and focus on the good and hopeful things that have happened over this year — especially over the past few months.
Peter, over 7 million of us took to the streets in October for ‘ No Kings Day ’ rallies to protest this administration’s undemocratic policies. Just a few weeks later, Democrats swept the nation. Both Abigail Spanberger in Virginia and Mikie Sherrill in New Jersey won their respective gubernatorial elections by double digit margins. Proposition 50 in California succeeded with millions of votes. Over 100 candidates with backgrounds in STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) were elected to state and local offices across the nation. The Pennsylvania Supreme Court won a Democratic majority. Here in Minnesota, Amanda Hemmingsen-Jaeger won her campaign for State Senate, helping the DFL keep its slim majority. And we have an incredible slate of candidates for the state legislature that are either stepping up to run or running for re-election in 2026. Peter, the future is looking bright!
These times make me reflect on my first campaign for the Minnesota legislature back in 2018. In the wake of Donald Trump’s first election, I raised my hand to run for office because I knew what a Trump presidency would mean for women’s healthcare and reproductive rights. The incumbent I ran against had won her last election by 20 points and there were plenty of people who thought flipping that seat would be impossible.
But I was determined and so was the hard working and committed network of people behind me — supporters just like you — who knocked on doors, called voters, and donated their time and treasure to flip that seat. And one conversation at a time, we broke through and beat a three term Republican incumbent and won a district that had never been represented by a Democrat before.
We now have an opponent and it promises to be a tough campaign. We’re ready — we’ve run and won tough races before, but we cannot underestimate the Republicans' plans and determination to maintain their majority. They will try to distract us from the corruption and cruelty of this administration and its Republican majorities in Congress, but we have to stay focused on winning next November so Democrats can win the majority and Congress can reclaim its authority as an equal branch of government.
I am focused on doing all I can to win re-election to this seat, and I need your help.
Tonight marks our biggest fundraising deadline of the campaign so far. At the beginning of the month, my team set a goal to raise $50,000 by December 31st. Once my opponent announced, we raised that goal to $75,000, and we are so close to closing this gap and hitting our goal. This grassroots team continues to astound me with their generosity, and every dollar raised goes towards holding my seat and running a strong campaign here in Minnesota that uplifts Democrats up and down the ballot, AND supports candidates who could flip the U.S. House in 2026.
I know this is an ambitious goal, but there is too much at stake to not give it our all. What do you say, Peter — could you contribute any amount today to help us reach our goal?

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.
