_Hey folks, it 's Mike. I'm taking a few days off with family to close out the year, but in my place today is someone I admire deeply--my friend, Mallory McMorrow._
_She 's running for U.S. Senate in Michigan, and she's written a brilliant piece about why Democrats don't have to settle anymore. I really hope you'll take a moment to read it--it perfectly captures what the party needs to do to win in 2026._
_**[And if you're fired up after reading, Mallory's got an end-of-year FEC fundraising deadline tonight. You can chip in any amount at this link to help her keep building momentum and win this race.](https://substack.com/redirect/5eefd9e1-e08b-4dc7-b139-6a47973b2ece?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
_Thanks, and see you in the new year._
* * *
Look, I get it.
It's hard not to feel repulsed by what we see happening across our county - institutions torn down to the studs, norms broken, so-called leadership in the White House more focused on padding their own pockets and promoting themselves than serving Americans. And while there have been moments of clarity and strength, there's still a nagging feeling that _this_ Democratic party wasn't built to meet this moment.
Meanwhile, you're at the grocery store and your bill is somehow $200 for what used to cost $100. Your rent just went up again. And that dream of owning a house? Yeah, that's starting to feel like it'll stay a dream forever.
I'm Mallory McMorrow. I'm the Senate Majority Whip here in Michigan. Maybe you saw that speech I gave back in 2022, or the Redzone ad from my Senate campaign. But honestly, I'm not here to talk about any of that today.
I want to talk about why we're all so tired of this, and why we don't have to accept it.
## **" When Was the Last Time They Had to Buy Groceries?"**
A few months back, I sat down with a group of union apprentices. These are young people doing everything right--learning trades, working hard, building real skills. And they absolutely laid into me.
"This whole system is corrupt," one told me. "Politicians are all rich. They're all 80 years old. When was the last time they had to buy a house? When is the last time they even drove their own car? How could they possibly know what we're going through?"
And you know what? He's right. He's absolutely right.
I graduated college straight into the Great Recession. I had a degree in my hand and no job prospects in front of me. I was crippled by student loan debt, had no health insurance (the ACA didn't exist yet). I worked retail for minimum wage. I know _exactly_ what it feels like to do everything right and feeling, crushingly, like it doesn't matter.
Here's the thing: Democrats don't have a shortage of good ideas. What we have is a shortage of leaders who actually understand what it's like to be most Americans today. I'd venture to guess there aren't many in power who remember what it's like to check your bank account before getting gas, or who have had to choose between going to the doctor and paying a bill.
That's why people are cynical. Not because they don't care about politics--but because they don't see themselves in the people claiming to represent them.
## **We Don 't Have to Play Small**
In 2018, I decided to run for State Senate in a Republican stronghold district in Oakland County, the suburbs just north of Detroit. And I decided to run against the sitting Republican incumbent who had won his previous election by 16 points...a long shot for even an experienced candidate, let alone a first-time candidate.
Some local Democratic party leaders were... let's say, not the most encouraging. One told me, "Oh honey, that's cute."
Well here's what we did with no expectations and "cute..."
But here's the thing about having no expectations: you're free. Free to build the campaign you believe in.
We organized 500 volunteers--retired teachers, high school kids, working parents. We knocked on doors. We listened.
And on Election Night 2018, we won. By four points.
That's why I will never accept it when someone tells me something "can't be done." We can organize everywhere. We can talk to our neighbors. We can win. Because people are looking for leaders who see them, listen to them, and will actually fight for them.
And we didn't win by playing it safe or triangulating our message into meaningless mush. We won by showing up everywhere, talking like actual human beings, and listening.
What drove our win in 2018? It wasn't a single issue. There was no magic buzzword.
On thousands of doorsteps and in countless conversations, I heard the same refrain over and over again: "You remind me a lot of my daughter, who left Michigan. Why are you here? And what can we do so my kids can stay?"
That became the umbrella for everything we focused on: education, civil rights, protecting our water, diversifying our economy, creating more opportunities and investing in communities.
From there, I helped Democrats flip the Michigan Senate for the first time in 40 years. Not by following the same old playbook. Not by deferring to "the way things have always been done." But by refusing to accept those limitations in the first place.
Voters are _hungry_ for this. They want authenticity. They want leaders who get what they're going through. They want a Democratic Party that fights as hard as the moment demands.
## **The Stakes Are Everything**
And let's be clear about what we're up against. Trump and his MAGA movement aren't just wrong about policy. They're actively trying to convince Americans that government is the enemy, that democracy is rigged, that we should just give up on the idea that politics can make our lives better.
The only way to fight that cynicism is by proving them wrong. Not with poll-tested messages or cautiously worded statements. But by delivering real results and talking about them like real people.
We need leaders who know what gas costs in 2025, not 1995. We need leaders who've dealt with the nightmare of finding affordable childcare. We need leaders who've helped aging parents navigate getting older, who have found themselves sandwiched between taking care of children and parents and wondering how to make it all work. We need leaders who remember what it's like to worry about money, to feel like the system is rigged against you, to wonder if your kids will ever have it as good as you did.
I'm not saying we should throw out experience. I'm saying we need to combine institutional knowledge with lived experience and fresh energy. We need to stop accepting "this is just how things work" when how things work is clearly failing most Americans.
## **Desperate for Something Real**
My 2022 speech went viral because people were so starved for a Democrat with a backbone that when they finally saw one, it resonated. People are _desperate_ for authenticity in politics. They want leaders who will call out BS when they see it and fight back when it matters, who get angry at things worth being angry about, who aren't afraid to lead while acknowledging that _nothing_ about this moment is normal, who don't act like this is business as usual.
Politics doesn't have to be boring. It can be engaging, even fun, while still being serious about the issues that matter. We can show up everywhere, listen first, and still deliver on the big stuff.
## **What Are We Going to Do About It?**
So here we are. The Democratic Party is at a crossroads.
We can keep accepting that we're supposed to lose in certain places. Keep nominating the same types of candidates who've been losing. Keep communicating in ways that make people's eyes glaze over. Keep prioritizing process over results, mistaking activity for achievement.
Or we can demand better.
We can insist on leaders who understand normal people because they _are_ normal people. We can expect our party to fight as hard for our values as Republicans fight for theirs. We can refuse to accept that good policy is enough--we also need to be able to explain why it matters in ways that reflect people's actual lives.
We saw sweeping victories for Democrats across the country this year - from Virginia to New Jersey to New York to Miami to Mississippi to Iowa to Pennsylvania.
What did they have in common? They didn't just point out what Trump and MAGA Republicans are doing wrong. They stayed relentlessly focused on affordability and offered something _better._
The choice is ours. We can settle for the status quo and hope things work out. Or we can build something better.
I know which one I'm choosing.
What about you?
-- Mallory

As the year comes to a close, I want to take a moment to explain why I’m running, and why this moment matters.
I’m not the candidate backed by Tennessee’s political elite, and I’m not swimming in establishment money or answering to insiders who think they can hand-pick our leaders. I’m a dad, a music industry veteran, and a person whose life was shaped by the supportive community around me.
I’m running because working families are getting pushed out while politicians protect themselves and their donors. I’ve lived what happens when leaders fail you, and I refuse to accept a system where corruption is tolerated and regular people are told to wait their turn.
This campaign is about accountability. It’s about standing up for families who feel ignored and building something strong enough to take on the insiders who think this seat belongs to them.
But we cannot do that if we fall short at this first major test. This report will shape how seriously our campaign is taken going into the election year, and we can’t fall short.
[**If you believe in what we’re building and want to help keep this campaign moving forward, please chip in before the deadline. Every contribution brings us closer to proving that this movement has real strength.**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/GdTnkiGdqhc34mUFMkd4Tg~~/AAUS1hA~/hw-CGdYmDxBGj-30Aza3P-ok5L_mf25baKPx7O44dFrL5P58m7vuI_kmOKDpK0F1bHv2nFjp7l_RPfVqynJTQLrOj-EsK_G7hUHry5SIl0cSH-rn7GgA1lUuGR968FyGURWthNm89DJ__rYOktKhfGDRL5J6GZP0EmputEDf3Ba-6hoTA9xjh_Hj1Jbs9nEN)
Thank you for being part of this fight,
Mike

# Happy 2026 Michigan!
---
| | Dear Friend and Patriot,
As we close out 2025 and welcome the promise of a new year, I want to wish you and your family a very Happy New Year! May 2026 bring you health, happiness, joy, and the blessings of faith, family, and freedom.
What will freedom look like? Just one year from now on January 1, 2027 - Inauguration Day - our weak Democrat Governor, Secretary of State, and Attorney General will officially be out work and it’s an unprecedented opportunity to **make Michigan red again**. [In just the past few hours, over 8,000 people watched this scene and can’t wait for this to happen](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=98c3fcfd10&e=4b10910eed):
[](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=e2ce298df7&e=4b10910eed)
As we head into the March GOP endorsement convention and the general election in November, your continued support and partnership will help us to [**keep growing our momentum to make the Michigan AG’s office ruby red again! Please consider a year-end donation to help us hit the ground running in 2026**](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=f4e39d162a&e=4b10910eed)**before 12:00 AM!**
[](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=6fb7250e28&e=4b10910eed)
As Michigan’s next Attorney General, I’ll hit the ground running alongside a strong conservative ticket on January 1, 2027 to stop political lawfare, protect your constitutional rights, support law enforcement, protect parental rights, defend your second amendment rights, ensure election integrity, stop unelected Lansing bureaucrats from converting our farmland into solar / wind / data center eyesores, and **put Michiganders first**.
I’m the only AG candidate in this race that fought our current Democrat AG and won multiple times, and the only AG candidate that actively took a stand on these issues at the time it mattered when others remained silent (their inaction is action - and it’s unacceptable).
[With President Trump’s steadfast support for Michigan that was personally shared with me the White House earlier this month](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=9a1a610963&e=4b10910eed), and your continued partnership, **we’ll make Michigan red again in 2026**!
---
| | **Happy New Year and Let’s Keep Winning!**
Kevin Kijewski
Republican Candidate for Michigan Attorney General

subject: A new kind of politics to save American democracy

body:
Real progress is built through grassroots organizing and relationship building.

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | | Happy New Year’s Eve, Friends!
You may have noticed that our emails look a little different than other campaigns.
Saikat has committed to never spam you with endless appeals asking for money. In fact, we debated whether we should send this second fundraising email out!
But we heard from many folks who meant to donate and appreciated the reminder.
So we wanted to let you know we’re only a few hours away from closing the books on 2025, and we need a few more supporters to help hit our end-of-year goal.
**We’re hoping to break 10,000 donations before the clock strikes midnight, but we’re not quite there yet.**[**Can you chip in $5 – or whatever you can afford – to help push us over the finish line?**](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=7d4c8d22c3&e=bf17056ae8)
---
| [CHIP IN NOW »](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=cfe1eda43b&e=bf17056ae8)
---
| | We need a new kind of politics to save American democracy and fight for working families – but in order for that to happen, **we need to show the establishment we have the grassroots support to win.**
As Saikat’s career working with AOC, Bernie, and Justice Democrats shows, real progress is built through grassroots organizing. It’s personal relationships, tens of thousands of conversations with friends, family, and neighbors that will bring the change San Franciscans are demanding.
**If you’ve been considering supporting Saikat’s campaign, now is the time.**[**Chip in today, and help us build a democracy and Democratic party that won’t just defeat MAGA, but will tangibly improve the lives of working people everywhere.**](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=b2618c8da7&e=bf17056ae8)
Gratefully,-Team Saikat
---
| [DONATE NOW »](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=86431bb2df&e=bf17056ae8)
---
|
---
| | | | | | Saikat Chakrabarti was Bernie’s Tech Director, AOC’s first chief of staff, founded Justice Democrats, and helped bring the Green New Deal to life. He’s running for Congress to build a San Francisco that works for everyone—teachers, immigrants, service workers, and everyone else who makes this city the best in the world.
If you believe San Franciscans deserve affordable housing, universal healthcare, climate resilience, and public power: [volunteer](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=b65bab1abd&e=bf17056ae8) with us and learn more about our campaign on our [website](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=3600d564a2&e=bf17056ae8).
Email is a critical way we stay in touch with our grassroots team, but if you’d prefer to stop receiving emails, [click here to unsubscribe](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/unsubscribe?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=95823b04c2&t=b&e=bf17056ae8&c=862089481d).

clean_body: | | | Hey Peter, we’re the WFP staff pets. We know we’re a little late to the holiday party, but we couldn’t let 2025 end without dropping by to say hi: While we’re here, we’ve got a tiny reminder: there’s still time to help our humans at WFP finish the year strong! Every dollar moves our humans closer to big wins in 2026: electing more WFP champions in every state and at every level of government, defending friends in Congress, and building a governing force that works for working people , not billionaires. Next year, our humans are on a mission: chasing down Trump’s allies in Congress and across state and local offices who are making life less affordable, less safe, and more uncertain for working families. They’re also sniffing out establishment and corporate Democrats who aren’t really fighting back. And with your help, we can win early races — from special elections to spring primaries, including a critical New Jersey congressional primary as early as February — and keep building the pack power we need to flip more seats away from Trump and corporate interests at every level of government. Thanks for sticking with us this year! And from all of us at WFP, happy new year! — The WFP Staff Pets (with a little help from our humans) Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. subject: Not sending this message to everyone

body:
Hey Peter, James here.
I’m not sending this email out to millions of people. It’s only going to a smaller number of folks like you who haven’t made a contribution to our U.S. Senate campaign yet.
I need to ask a favor, and I’m hoping you’re someone who can help.
You’ve likely heard that there’s an official FEC deadline tonight for campaigns like ours. It may not seem like a big deal — and yes, it’s quite inconvenient to have to do this on New Year’s Eve.
But it’s a major test for the movement we’re trying to build. After our first full-quarter of fundraising, our numbers are legally required to be made public. People will look at them to gauge the strength of our campaign, but right now, we’re short of where I had hoped we’d be at this point in the day.
That’s why I am turning to you. I want to show that we’re only getting stronger just when it matters most. Everyone who becomes a Founding Donor before the year ends sends a powerful message just when it matters most.
**[Please consider using this link to make your first contribution to our campaign for U.S. Senate. It would mean the world to me to know you have my back heading into 2026.](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-launch.bF5RK3&refcode=em251231-2-ak&t=1&akid=363%2E1347274%2EKzvPDN)**

Again I’m not making this request of millions of people, so anything you can do would make an extraordinary difference.
Thank you.
James

# Happy Last Day of 2025!
---
| | Most people spend their time over the holidays catching up on a good book, on sleep, or binge-watching their favorite shows.
But me? I’m hard at work to make sure we are set up to win this campaign! And I honestly wouldn’t have it any other way!
---
|
---
| | Nothing is more important to me than saving our democracy, standing up for what’s right, and making sure everyone can enjoy a stress-free holiday without fear of persecution or how they’re going to afford their everyday needs.
As many of you know, I’m a big data nerd, and I wanted to share something very exciting I uncovered this week.
Under the new Texas maps, CD21 has lost 75 precincts and gained 86 new ones - 68 of which are in San Antonio and 58 of which are super blue and used to be in Representative Castro’s district. I was proudly endorsed by Rep. Castro in our last campaign, and I’m proudly endorsed by him again!
**I KNOW we can win this!** I was made for this fight, and I’m ready for this fight!
This always has been and always will be a people-powered campaign. As we approach our end of year fundraising deadline, I’m asking you to answer the call.
If you haven’t yet donated, please [**make a contribution today before midnight**](https://drkristinhook.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fd888d2bb4a2d4cad917af4b9&id=8591f4b16b&e=395a33a3d2) to become an early supporter and help us flip this seat once and for all!
Have a fun and safe end to your year, and I’ll see y’all on the other side!
---

subject: Happy New Year from Autism Health!
body:
Happy New Year from Autism Health Inc.

As we welcome a brand new year, all of us at Autism Health Inc. want to extend our heartfelt gratitude to you. Your support, your belief in our mission, and your commitment to families impacted by autism have made 2025 a year of meaningful progress and hope.

This past year, we have been blessed to build incredible partnerships with organizations and leaders who share our vision. These collaborations are already creating new opportunities, resources, and pathways of support for individuals with autism and other neurological disorders. We are deeply grateful to everyone who has supported our mission to make this all possible.

And we are just getting started. We have exciting announcements, new programs, and additional partnerships on the horizon for the coming year. Together, we will continue to advance education, research, and community support that truly make a difference.

>From our Autism Health family to yours, we wish you a joyful and healthy New Year filled with many blessings. May 2026 bring growth, healing, and new beginnings for us all.

With gratitude,
Steve & Tracy Slepcevic
Founders of Autism Health Inc.

Adopt-A-Family for the Holidays!

Support Families. Restore Hope. Change Lives.

This holiday season, Autism Health & Dr. Goodenowe Enterprises are launching our Adopt-A-Family initiative to help children and adults with autism access care that can truly change the trajectory of their lives. Many families in our community are struggling... financially, emotionally, and physically. But too often, the resources they need are out of reach.

To meet this need, we have partnered with Dr. Goodenowe Enterprises and the Dr. Goodenowe Community Health Initiative to provide families with a comprehensive support system that includes plasmalogen precursor supplementation, community education, monthly mentorship, and guidance from trained navigators who walk alongside families every step of the way.

These programs are already helping individuals experience improvements in focus, communication, sleep, mood, anxiety levels, and overall daily functioning. When you adopt a family for the holidays, you are directly funding access to this full restorative support system.

Here is the link to the recent press release with more details...
PRESS RELEASE (https://world.einnews.com/pr_news/877481253/dr-dayan-goodenowe-and-autism-health-announce-dr-goodenowe-childhood-neurodevelopmental-support-program-neurosupport?mc_cid=dcd008325f&mc_eid=UNIQID)

How You Can Help

By adopting a family, you provide three months or more of life-changing support, including:

• Plasmalogen precursor supplements

• Access to the Engage community platform

• Monthly mentorship through the Community Health Navigator program

• Education, guidance, and community connection

Whether you support one individual or multiple families, your contribution will bring hope and stability to those who need it most this holiday season.
DONATE HERE (https://givebutter.com/goodenowe?gbtid=145aa5eb-55ab-435c-bf02-41ab0d50b2a9&mc_cid=dcd008325f&mc_eid=UNIQID)

** Autism Health Summit 2026 – Last Month for Discounted Tickets
------------------------------------------------------------

The countdown is on! This is the final month to purchase your tickets to the Autism Health Summit 2026 at the discounted rate. Beginning January 5th, ticket prices will increase by $50, so now is the perfect time to secure your spot.

For this month only, you can take an additional $25 off your ticket with promo code Holiday25 at checkout.

Join us April 24–26, 2026 at the beautiful Legacy Center Resort & Spa in San Diego, California, for a powerful three-day event that brings together leading voices in advocacy, research, and integrative health.

Our headline speakers for the Autism Health Summit bring exceptional expertise and leadership to the stage. We are honored to welcome Aaron Siri, Esq., a nationally recognized medical freedom attorney; Del Bigtree, an investigative journalist and host of The HighWire; and Dr. Toby Rogers, a respected researcher and public health analyst. Their combined insight, advocacy, and commitment to truth make this year’s Summit one of our most powerful lineups yet.

Seats are limited, and the Summit is expected to sell out. Reserve your spot today and be part of a transformative weekend of education, empowerment, and community.

Autism Health provides educational programs, workshops, events, research, and resources tailored to meet the diverse needs of those impacted by autism and other neurological disorders.

clean_body: Happy New Year from Autism Health Inc. As we welcome a brand new year, all of us at Autism Health Inc. want to extend our heartfelt gratitude to you. Your support, your belief in our mission, and your commitment to families impacted by autism have made 2025 a year of meaningful progress and hope. This past year, we have been blessed to build incredible partnerships with organizations and leaders who share our vision. These collaborations are already creating new opportunities, resources, and pathways of support for individuals with autism and other neurological disorders. We are deeply grateful to everyone who has supported our mission to make this all possible. And we are just getting started. We have exciting announcements, new programs, and additional partnerships on the horizon for the coming year. Together, we will continue to advance education, research, and community support that truly make a difference. From our Autism Health family to yours, we wish you a joyful and healthy New Year filled with many blessings. May 2026 bring growth, healing, and new beginnings for us all. With gratitude, Steve & Tracy Slepcevic Founders of Autism Health Inc. Adopt-A-Family for the Holidays! Support Families. Restore Hope. Change Lives. This holiday season, Autism Health & Dr. Goodenowe Enterprises are launching our Adopt-A-Family initiative to help children and adults with autism access care that can truly change the trajectory of their lives. Many families in our community are struggling... financially, emotionally, and physically. But too often, the resources they need are out of reach. To meet this need, we have partnered with Dr. Goodenowe Enterprises and the Dr. Goodenowe Community Health Initiative to provide families with a comprehensive support system that includes plasmalogen precursor supplementation, community education, monthly mentorship, and guidance from trained navigators who walk alongside families every step of the way. These programs are already helping individuals experience improvements in focus, communication, sleep, mood, anxiety levels, and overall daily functioning. When you adopt a family for the holidays, you are directly funding access to this full restorative support system. Here is the link to the recent press release with more details... Our headline speakers for the Autism Health Summit bring exceptional expertise and leadership to the stage. We are honored to welcome Aaron Siri, Esq., a nationally recognized medical freedom attorney; Del Bigtree, an investigative journalist and host of The HighWire; and Dr. Toby Rogers, a respected researcher and public health analyst. Your support gives me hope that we can build a better future and a stronger community together.| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/122382247/592420660/-1283252511?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTllYjQ2MjEtN2ZlNi1mMDExLTgxOTUtMDAwZDNhMWQ1OGFhIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=tb78rRY-e85pu5htKEs3wlL2w3Gl5UkItOS3736OBxo=&emci=52ba6f57-5ee6-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&emdi=19eb4621-7fe6-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&ceid=12466492)

| | Friend,
---
As we welcome a new year, I would like to take a moment to thank you for all that you do. Your support gives me hope that we can build a better future and a stronger community together.
---
To put it plainly, 2025 was hard for many. But it reminded me that we can face hard moments when we come together and lead with kindness, compassion, and a steadfast commitment to one another.
---
I know the year ahead will bring its own challenges. With clear eyes, I’m ready to continue our work because Rhode Islanders deserve leadership that shows up, listens, and fights for fairness, opportunity, and dignity.
---
Despite everything, I remain optimistic. Your encouragement, generosity, resilience, and hope are what help to make progress possible, even in difficult times. Your example is why I’m looking ahead to the new year in service of our shared values.
---
Wishing you and your loved ones peace, good health, and brighter days ahead.
---
Happy New Year,Gabe

name: Christopher Ahuja for Congress
subject: ACA Subsidies Expire at Midnight. Premiums Go Up Tomorrow.
body:
Help us fight for healthcare!

| | | | | [|
---](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=c5a38ec760&e=53c7d12fc7)
| | | | | | Dear Peter,Tomorrow, millions of Americans will face the reality of higher health care costs — bigger premiums, and for some, they will have to go without healthcare — too expensive under the Trump administration. Affordable Care Act subsidies are expiring today at midnight, and the result will be painful for working families, seniors, and small business owners who rely on the ACA to afford coverage.This outcome was 100% preventable. The Republicans in Congress failed to act in the best interest of the American people. Again. Amendments were offered multiple times to extend the subsidies and protect families from sticker shock. Brad Sherman had every opportunity to stand up and fight for relief, to work with colleagues in a bipartisan manner, to raise hell while Republicans rip healthcare away from cancer patients, dialysis recipients, children with treatable illnesses. Once again, when it mattered most, he stayed silent.As we welcome the new year, families will be forced to make impossible choices between health care, rent, groceries, and gas. Seniors on fixed incomes will struggle. Small business owners will face new uncertainty — while corporate interests continue to receive special treatment and bigger bank accounts. I believe Congress has a responsibility to act — not posture, delay, or disappear like they did. Leadership means showing up and fighting for the people you represent, especially when the clock is running out. Especially when it’s people’s healthcare. California’s 32nd Congressional District deserves a representative who will protect affordable health care. Tomorrow didn’t have to look like this. And next year doesn’t have to either.[**Join me in fighting for what’s right.**](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=25a7f4af8c&e=53c7d12fc7)

Friend, it's Heidi.
There's only one thing that really matters when it comes to helping us flip this seat and kicking Kiley out of Congress:
Your support.
The toxic politics of the Republican Party, and Kevin Kiley in particular, aim to divide us and make everything about "the red team" winning and "the blue team" losing.
But, Friend, there are no teams.
It's just us.
Our district, our communities, and our neighbors, who are all being left behind by the divisive politics of Trump and careerists like Kevin Kiley.
I say it's your support that matters most because while our opponents may have corporate PACs and billionaires who love dividing our country bankrolling their campaigns— I refuse to sell out our communities for money.
That's why, Friend, with our End of Year Fundraising Deadline in just 12 hours, I need your help. Can you chip in any amount that you can to help us raise the $3,145 we need to reach our 2025 goal before midnight tonight? Heidi Hall has spent her three-decade public service career working with others to solve problems, protect our land and water, improve health, and build opportunities for others, all while raising two boys primarily as a single mom.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20251231_em_fr_b1_HH_big [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20251231_em_fr_b1_HH_big]
Raised by parents who had persisted to make a middle-class life for their kids in Contra Costa County while lifting up others, Heidi was taught to push through and overcome challenges rather than complain about them. She learned to stick up for the vulnerable, to respect working people, and to value equal opportunity and justice.
After graduating from Pomona College and earning graduate degrees from Columbia and Rutgers, Heidi went to work for the Rockefeller Foundation promoting reproductive care and then began her career at the Environmental Protection Agency, stopping the dumping of toxic waste and holding corporate polluters accountable.
Today, Heidi chairs the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, where she’s taken on homelessness, expanded broadband access, and worked to reduce crime and illegal cannabis growth. Heidi flipped her seat from red to blue – and now she’s ready to do it again in Congress to take on toxic politics in Washington and put people first.

subject: This will be the last time I reach out this year.
body:

body:
Hi again,
In just hours, the year comes to a close—and so does our chance to enter the new year ready to fight for climate justice.
Because of supporters like you, we’ve pushed back against polluters, organized communities, and demanded real climate solutions. But the work ahead is even bigger.
If you can, please make a generous last-minute gift to OLCV before midnight tonight. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/t28-fgcXRUmjEwNoP96SgQ2] You have less than 12 hours! Your donation helps power climate action when it matters most.

Every contribution—no matter the size—helps us protect our planet and our future. Thank you for standing with us.
In solidarity,

Dear Peter,
I hope you are having a wonderful holiday season so far. I’m interrupting your break today to remind you that while the rest of the world seems to be on pause now, the climate crisis is not — and neither is OLCV.
Because of our supporters like you, this past year we:
* Pushed legislators to act on climate through lobbying, advocacy days, and emails to lawmakers;
* Demanded accountability from lawmakers on their climate inaction;
* And exceeded our 2025 member action goal by over 4,000!
None of this happened by accident. It happened because people like you chose action over silence, and making a gift to OLCV today is what gets it started [https://secure.ngpvan.com/t28-fgcXRUmjEwNoP96SgQ2] .
Right now, we’re facing a critical moment. The decisions made in the coming months will shape our climate future for decades. To meet this challenge, we need to enter the new year strong — and that depends on your support today.
Will you make a generous end-of-year gift of $50 or $100 to OLCV before midnight on December 31st? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/t28-fgcXRUmjEwNoP96SgQ2] Your contribution fuels organizing, advocacy, and rapid response, at a time when our climate is under threat. With Trump in the White House, what we can accomplish at the state level is increasingly vital for ensuring a sustainable and livable future for all.
Make a gift [https://secure.ngpvan.com/t28-fgcXRUmjEwNoP96SgQ2?am=50&contactdata=zFLFb1hHqWzgJC1DLM8Lxhyo7oRtzVY3DYOU2uo/2JbtivSlAhEBSDzZJ/LGVGdU/EHNz0TvU7z4Wl/0S4gaEn9Mi6rTHDCjPLRF4THcZyWGqOFuDn3ZYLHNiMsr3wxH]
Every dollar you give today helps us push harder and have a greater impact for a livable future. No matter what you’re able to give, your gift matters. It’s an investment in clean energy, environmental justice, and hope.
Thank you for standing with us this year. Together, we’re building a future where people and the planet come first.
With determination,

Dear Peter, I’m inspired by the progress we’ve been able to make together in my first term as Governor. And because I know there’s so much more yet to do, I’m ready to work hard next year to ask Oregonians to grant me the honor of serving the state for another four years. I’m only able to do that with your support. [**Will you support me with a donation of $10?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/122386749/592432202/-780220320?amount=10&refcode=AU_TK_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20251231_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3ZjkyMzE2YS04NWU2LWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XRQj6VR-l3kqqAv_vsDQOfmbRn4ZZWUc7r8M0trwsFU=) | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/122386751/592432203/-780220320?refcode=AU_TK_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20251231_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3ZjkyMzE2YS04NWU2LWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XRQj6VR-l3kqqAv_vsDQOfmbRn4ZZWUc7r8M0trwsFU=)
---
I want to build on the progress we’ve been making. During my first (almost) three years, here are some things we’ve accomplished:
\- We’ve added 6,286 new shelter beds to help people have more stability than the streets and we’ve helped 25,942 households from losing their homes and experiencing homelessness.
\- We’ve put everyday people first by taking action to make life more affordable by lowering prescription drug costs, protecting families from rising utility costs, shielding families from having their credit ruined by medical debt, and stopping predatory auto loans.
**I’m no nonsense and have no tolerance for partisan bickering.** I’ve worked across the aisle to get the important things done — like paying our firefighters after a terrible wildfire season, expanding summer reading programs, and more.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

We’re tired of everybody burying this story. It’s time to get loud about it. Because when these scumbags get rich, Veterans will die. The only way we can stop that is by coming together and forcing them.
#
Peter,
Writing to make sure you saw the news that Trump and VA Secretary Collins are eliminating 35,000 health care jobs — doctors and nurses — at the VA.
That’s after they cut 30,000 jobs already. Whatever staff are left are overworked without any hope of relief. Clinics and hospitals are understaffed. In many cases, it’s doctors and nurses working the phones because all of the administrative staff were cut.
We made a promise to Veterans — you serve us, and we will serve you. We are breaking that promise. And it’s important to be clear about why:
It’s not just because these people are evil. Not just because they’re liars, cheats, and crooks — though that’s a part of it. It’s because they don’t want the VA to exist in its current state.
They haven’t been able to figure out how to get rich off of battered Veterans yet. They want service to get worse, they want people waiting longer for worse care. They want all of that so they can justify selling off the VA to some private health care provider owned by their rich friends — and make millions off the stock trades.
We’re tired of everybody burying this story. It’s time to get loud about it. Because when these scumbags get rich, Veterans will die. The only way we can stop that is by coming together and forcing them.
VoteVets has fought off VA privatization schemes for two decades, but this one is unlike any other. It’s the greatest threat to health care for Veterans in any of our lifetimes, and we’ve got to start fighting back.

Hi Peter,
This year changed me.
I started 2025 with a good tech job. My work on the Skokie school board was the most fulfilling thing I'd ever done. Helping students. Supporting families. Showing up for my neighbors.
Then Trump was sworn in. Agencies eliminated. Education is gutted. Tariffs that drove prices up overnight and pushed families to the brink. ICE kidnapping my neighbors.
I was volunteering. Organizing. Doing what I could to resist. But I couldn't shake the thought: I can do more. No, I have to do more.
When Rep.Jan Schakowsky announced her retirement, I didn't see a "career move." I saw a responsibility. Washington has been shaped for too long by politicians who answer to corporations and special interests instead of the people who have to live with the consequences of their actions.
So I took the leap.
---
| [](https://e96gjzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001drTXKhHfzzPCu_TOO--6paDiKFSFwmFfEgBMOoKVVmMHNxKlcY_FhdHohYj9MXHiQyRC-QR1EIdasKlVfjSMGQspObn6YTBxsu9RwOketxMhMgwNxpSqYb0OONT3kp4XrAQ_f1VzecXI5gJPFAA3hanSdqDbrEs6dbRJq5GdW8jRYKAtCA2wVS0lDJ-ipOMUX9F1FNqRyzrnS_Fxcahmx2nrrBc6Dxew&c=TnB8lgvkVNbYFyXV9UqChXKYZ6KC41yUqAnktgiFYJEKvXua3GoQTQ==&ch=vXmM_Q7UVTVQe7jaqKN1FYS9nqTUCIAuCt34mWZsMV0cPb30bD0YnQ==)
---

In June, I started crisscrossing Illinois' 9th Congressional District, listening to the concerns of my neighbors at kitchen tables, in community centers, heck even garages. As the campaign went on, I was genuinely overwhelmed by what began to happen.
Word spread. People showed up. Our campaign quickly became one of the top-funded in the race because of thousands of small dollar donors. Hundreds of volunteers signed up. Events filled. I quit my job to focus on this campaign full-time. And before long, the momentum started to snowball in a way that reminded me: this isn't about me. It's about a community deciding to stand up together.

---
| [](https://e96gjzhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001drTXKhHfzzPCu_TOO--6paDiKFSFwmFfEgBMOoKVVmMHNxKlcY_FhdHohYj9MXHiQyRC-QR1EIdasKlVfjSMGQspObn6YTBxsu9RwOketxMhMgwNxpSqYb0OONT3kp4XrAQ_f1VzecXI5gJPFAA3hanSdqDbrEs6dbRJq5GdW8jRYKAtCA2wVS0lDJ-ipOMUX9F1FNqRyzrnS_Fxcahmxy457cnzu8xR&c=TnB8lgvkVNbYFyXV9UqChXKYZ6KC41yUqAnktgiFYJEKvXua3GoQTQ==&ch=vXmM_Q7UVTVQe7jaqKN1FYS9nqTUCIAuCt34mWZsMV0cPb30bD0YnQ==)

But I am carrying that reminder of what a community can achieve when it stands together forward into the new year. clean_body: | | | | | == | Hi Peter, This year changed me. I started 2025 with a good tech job. My work on the Skokie school board was the most fulfilling thing I'd ever done. Helping students. Supporting families. Showing up for my neighbors. Then Trump was sworn in. Agencies eliminated. Education is gutted. Tariffs that drove prices up overnight and pushed families to the brink. ICE kidnapping my neighbors. I was volunteering. Organizing. Doing what I could to resist. But I couldn't shake the thought: I can do more. No, I have to do more. When Rep.Jan Schakowsky announced her retirement, I didn't see a "career move." I saw a responsibility. Washington has been shaped for too long by politicians who answer to corporations and special interests instead of the people who have to live with the consequences of their actions. So I took the leap. | == In June, I started crisscrossing Illinois' 9th Congressional District, listening to the concerns of my neighbors at kitchen tables, in community centers, heck even garages. As the campaign went on, I was genuinely overwhelmed by what began to happen. Word spread. People showed up. Our campaign quickly became one of the top-funded in the race because of thousands of small dollar donors. Hundreds of volunteers signed up. Events filled. I quit my job to focus on this campaign full-time. And before long, the momentum started to snowball in a way that reminded me: this isn't about me. It's about a community deciding to stand up together. | == | As I look ahead to 2026, I am deeply concerned about outside groups like AIPAC who are trying to buy this seat. Our community deserves their next representative to be one that represents their interests, not billionaire donors or corporations. But I am carrying that reminder of what a community can achieve when it stands together forward into the new year. == | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | == | | == | | == | | == | | == | | == | == | If you can, make a donation of any amount. name: Dan Crenshaw
subject: Midnight Deadline: Don’t Let Democrats Define This Race
body:
https://secure.winred.com/crenshawforcongress/d6586a65fbe2ad7f

Peter,

Dan Crenshaw here—wishing you a Happy New Year and many blessings for you and your family in 2026.

I’m reaching out with a quick but important request. If you’re able, please consider supporting my re-election campaign before our End-of-Year deadline tonight at midnight.

[CONTRIBUTE NOW](https://secure.winred.com/crenshawforcongress/d6586a65fbe2ad7f)

Why does this deadline matter so much?

Because on January 15, every campaign must publicly report the total amount raised between October 1 and December 31. That number sends a clear message—either strength or weakness—to our opponents. It’s critical that we report a strong total and show Democrats that this campaign has real, unstoppable momentum.

And yes, that matters—even with the general election still months away.

Why?

Because just in the past month, Democrats have already spent over $100,000 flooding my district with dishonest television ads attacking my record of service. They’re doing this now because they’re afraid of what we’ve accomplished—and what we’re going to keep accomplishing.

They’re afraid because we’ve delivered real results:

- Reimbursing Texas for border security operations
- Leading the fight—alongside President Trump—against the Mexican cartels
- Passing legislation to ban taxpayer funding for gender-transition procedures on minors
- Advancing breakthrough research to treat veterans suffering from PTSD and TBI
Even Speaker Johnson has said I am “our point man in Congress when it comes to addressing the ongoing threat of the drug cartels.”

I’m proud of that record—and our work is far from finished.

Democrats know they can’t win this district outright, so they’re trying a familiar playbook: spend early, lie loudly, and interfere in GOP primaries to weaken strong, conservative candidates before voters ever get their say.

We cannot let them succeed.

[Any contribution you can make tonight—no matter the amount—will be put to immediate use setting the record straight, countering the attacks, and ensuring we’re fully prepared to protect this seat and defend the House this November.](https://secure.winred.com/crenshawforcongress/d6586a65fbe2ad7f)

Thank you, as always, for standing with me. I truly can’t do this without you.

Happy New Year,

https://secure.winred.com/crenshawforcongress/d6586a65fbe2ad7f

Dan Crenshaw

[CONTRIBUTE NOW](https://secure.winred.com/crenshawforcongress/d6586a65fbe2ad7f)

When Donald Trump called Colorado Gov. Jared Polis a "SLEAZEBAG" because Polis refused to roll over and release the convicted felon and election tamperer, Tina Peters, from state prison, Lauren Boebert eagerly applauded him.
When Trump uprooted Space Command HQ from Colorado, relocating it to Huntsville, Alabama at great expense to taxpayers for no other reason than loyalty to him and to MAGA, Boebert shrugged--and blamed Democrats.
When Trump declared he would dismantle the U.S. National Science Foundation's (NSF) National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR), hurting its 830 employees and life-saving climate science, Boebert stayed silent.
When Trump claimed without evidence or facts that mail-in voting was rife with fraud and abuse, Boebert nodded along. Colorado is a universal vote-by-mail state. Rural voters benefit greatly from mail-in voting. Trump himself casts a mail-in ballot in Florida.
Boebert was more than happy to see the MAGA monster she had a role in creating attack things she doesn't like: democracy, voting rights, abortion rights, you name it.
But now that Trump has harmed Boebert and the people she claims to care about and represent, Boebert is freaking out. The monster has turned on its creator.

## 2025 CAMPAIGN RECAP
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | Friends,
As we close out 2025, I want to share what you helped make possible this year. Karrin has been all over Arizona, meeting voters face-to-face, listening to families and small business owners, and building a campaign that will defeat Katie Hobbs and elect a Republican Governor who will Make Arizona Strong Again.
This year, Karrin completed **over 280 campaign stops and visited all 15 counties**. She showed up everywhere because Arizona deserves a Governor who does the work.
And together, we hit a historic milestone. Karrin has **raised the most money of any non-incumbent Republican candidate for Governor in Arizona history**. That is real momentum, and it is helping us build the strongest coalition possible heading into 2026.
This historic fundraising haul came from **more than 11,000 individual donors** , with an **average donation of $83**. That kind of grassroots support sends a clear message: Arizonans want secure borders, safer communities, and an economy that works for working families.
Thank you for being part of this fight. If you are ready to keep building, reply to this email to volunteer, host a meet-and-greet, or make an end-of-year contribution. Also, if you haven’t already, please sign Karrin’s petition by clicking the red button below!

_**by Ellie Leonard, BAM Contributing Editor**_
_**Trigger Warning: this article contains discussion of sexual abuse and sexual abuse of a minor.**_
When I was first researching Jeffrey Epstein, I came across Vicky Ward's 2003 article in Vanity Fair, titled "The Talented Mr. Epstein." I came away with a sick feeling that something wasn't being said in the cryptic, yet gushing description of the billionaire bachelor with a "70-acre island" and a "fleet of aircraft."
A 2019 article by the New York Times' Marc Tracy would answer that question, though vaguely, claiming Ward had by silenced by her editor. What Ward hadn't said was that three women had come forward to accuse Jeffrey Epstein, before the list, the files, the island, even before Me Too. Somehow, they had summoned the bravery to be the very first ones to tell a young journalist their story.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Annie and Maria Farmer, 1996 - Photo Credit: Maria Farmer
It began with Maria Farmer, 26, who worked for Jeffrey Epstein as an art advisor after he offered to help her painting career. While in college, the dean of the New York Academy of Art, Eileen Guggenheim, had introduced her to Epstein and his former girlfriend, Ghislaine Maxwell, telling the young artist to sell them a painting she'd done of a man staring at a woman on a sofa. Ms. Guggenheim later said she recalled no such interaction.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A painting by Maria Farmer that she says she was asked to sell to Jeffrey Epstein
Farmer would go on to acquire art for Epstein's massive Upper East Side mansion, later working the front desk, where she was the first and last eyes on every visitor coming in and out of Epstein's home. Some were models, often coming for "auditions for the lingerie retailer Victoria's Secret." Most were young.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ghislaine Maxwell - Getty Images
Farmer said Maxwell would go out in a car, hunting for young girls, whom she referred to as "nubiles." _This was the same term that would later pop up in a letter from Jeffrey Epstein to Larry Nassar, days before he was found dead in his jail cell._
> #### "They had a driver, and he would be driving along, and Ghislaine would say, 'Get that girl.' And they'd stop, and she'd run out and get the girl and talk to her." \- Maria Farmer
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Maria Farmer at Leslie Wexner's home in Ohio, 1996
At one point, Maria traveled to another of Epstein's properties in Ohio, inside a larger complex owned by Les Wexner, CEO of L Brands. One late summer night, both Epstein and Maxwell paid a visit, and Epstein asked her to massage his feet. She thought it strange, but he'd let her stay in his friend Wexner's sprawling mansion, so she did what he asked. He moaned like he was in pain, clearly pleasured, then invited her to sit on his bed and watch a PBS program about math. Again, awkward, but she did as he asked. Maxwell joined them on the bed, and soon both older adults were groping the young woman, to the point of bruising her nipples and doing everything in "unison, mirroring each other's movements." Farmer left the bed and locked herself in another room, calling her father and an art mentor on the phone for help. She would report everything to the police.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Jeffrey Epstein, James Brown, and Donald Trump
When Epstein became embroiled in his first sexual-assault-of-a-minor case, Farmer told a newspaper she'd been invited to an "impromptu meeting" in Epstein's office in 1995 when Donald Trump walked in.
> #### "Mr. Trump hovered over her and stared at her legs, making her feel scared." \- Cameron Henderson, the NY Times
Epstein noticed, too, and cleared the air. "She's not for you." The pair left, but Farmer heard Trump say he thought she looked about 16 years old. She was 25. It was her first and last experience with the future President. But something about it felt off, and when she was interviewed by the FBI about the case in 2006, she recommended they look into Epstein's relationship with Donald Trump. The FBI claim never to have had this conversation.
> #### "She's not for you." \- Jeffrey Epstein
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Maria and Annie Farmer, c. 1991
When Maria's younger sister, Annie, came to visit New York City, she got along quite well with Epstein. He even offered to mentor her and help her get into college. But when he took her to the movies one afternoon, he reached over to touch her in the dark. She was only 16.
_**The following are Annie 's redacted journal entries from 1996, released by the DOJ on December 23, 2025. She and her sister Maria have given me permission to name them in these entries.**_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_" I'm so excited. [MARIA'S] Boss bought me a ticket to come out and see her. it has been almost a year - scary. He is very wealthy and might help me get into or pay for college. I don't want to get my hopes up because I hate dissapointment [sic] but it would be really cool if it happened and even if it doesn't it is so great I get to go see her."_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_January 7, 1996_
_" I got back from my trip to NY today. I had such a great time it is really depressing to be back home. I feel like it was a trip that changed my whole outlook on life. I guess I always feel that way a little bit when I get back from trips - but it is overwhelming this time. I am so ready to be out of high school and in college. Everything seems to silly, - going out, etc - it did a little before anyway - I even feel a little isolated from my friends. Before I left I was on a high of how great my friends were. I still realize how wonderful they are but I feel more independent, like they aren't necessary. I felt like this when I got back from Mexico and it faded quickly but I have a feeling it is different this time. New York is such an amazing city. I felt really comfortable there - like I know that I belonged there and would live there at some point hopefully soon. I miss [MARIA] so much already it seems unfair that I can't see her more often. I feel like I'm missing so much. There is so much to tell about the trip I don't know where to begin. The best night was when [MARIA] and I saw Phantom of the Opera. We went to Jeff Epstein's house and had champagne w/ him. I found him down to earth and easy to talk to. I thanked him so much for the trip, etc. We then took..."_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"...his car - his driver actually took us to Phantom. I didn't know any play could be so moving. I had seen it before but still couldn't believe it. I balled [sic] - it was fantastic. After the play we walked around the Plaza and went home. It was so much fun. I met [MARIA'S] boyfriend and [REDACTED] he was different than I expected - pretty cute, nice, but they didn't get along very well at the beg(inning), which made me pretty annoyed w/ him. he turned out to be pretty cool once he chilled out. His brother [REDACTED] was 25 and we hung out with him a lot. at 1st I didn't think he was as cute as she had said but quickly found him really cute. We hung out for the 1st couple days than [sic] the 4 of us went to their cabin. We had a lot of fun, x-country skied, watched Sleuth (**** movie) and hung out. We had to sleep in the same bed and ended up talking for a really long time. I kind of wanted something to happen but didn't know I just thought he was cute and fun. I didn't see him again until Friday we went to a club to watch some bands, to a bar and then [MARIA] announced she was staying at Jeffreys and asked [REDACTED] to stay w/ me. I was secretly happy but didn't want him to think I had wanted her to do this so acted kind of upset. They left us at [REDACTED] w/ [REDACTED]. I wondered if he wanted..."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_" ...to [REDACTED] about it because she worships him and it would just create problems. I couldn't tell anyone else because it is not a big deal and I didn't want to portray him in a bad light. I really don't think it is a big deal. I think he is just a relaxed guy and likes to flirt,, or was being fatherly or something. I know this sounds like me trying to justify him doing something weird but it isn't. Right now my big concern is what I am going to do this summer. There are so many cool things to do and amazing places to go. Right now I am really thinking about doing something in Africa. It would be incredible - so different, so beautiful, all the different people I would love it. I think I will really be happy doing almost anything. I am entering, actually am in a pretty good period. This could all be over by tomorrow but I feel pretty happy right now and excited for the future, (not immediate - track and school), this summer, senior year, and college. I am having a lot of fun w/ [REDACTED] and [REDACTED]. We have so much fun doing things together. [MARIA] is having some problems and kind of alienating herself from everyone. I hope she gets over it. Things are also going well w/ [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] and I've been talking to [REDACTED] a little more although still not enough. It makes me a little sad to think about it and mad because it seems like she doesn't make much of an effort."_
Annie didn't write anything for another 18 days, but when she did it was clear her feelings about the trip to New York had changed.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_June 25, 1996_
_" It has been a couple of weeks since I got back and I have gotten back into the swing of things. A couple of quick details about NY I didn't mention earlier -- went to see The Duchess - a decent play, and Blue Man group (Tubes) off broadway really cool production. Went to the flea market where I got some cool stuff, went to Jeffrey Epstein's mansion, went to the Met, a pretty fun New Year's Eve party, went to thrift stores where I got an amazing dress for prom, it's from the fifties, lace with pink flowers w/ rhinestones in the middle all over it, it is my dream dress. One night we went to the movies w/ Jeffrey Epstein. It was a little weird one of those things that is hard to explain we were sitting next to each other and he put out his hand for me to hold and we were holding hands (not weird, normal and fine) then he kind of caressed/rubbed my arm and shoe/foot - It was one of those things that just gave me a weird feeling but wasn't that weird and probably normal - the one thing that kind of weirded me out about it was he let go of my hand when he was talking to [MARIA] - Well I decided it was no big deal, it just made me mad because he is being so amazing - paying for a summer program for me, helping me w/ college - he is so nice and so generous w/ everyone and I just didn't want to have any weird things about it - I didn't/couldn't say anything."_
Years later, Annie looked back on her first experience with Jeffrey Epstein at just 16 years old.
> #### "I felt sick to my stomach. It was not something I was expecting at all." \- Annie Farmer.
When he invited her to his massive New Mexico Ranch, she wasn't sure she wanted to go, but knowing Ghislaine Maxwell would be there she felt a little better about the idea, still hoping he could get her into a good college. So she went. And again, he took her to the movies, but this time with Maxwell in tow. Epstein reached over to grab the girl's hand, rubbing her feet and the sides of her arms, hiding nothing from the older woman who sat beside them.
When they arrived back at the property, Maxwell offered to give the girl a massage. Still so naive, she trusted the women. Maxwell "pulled down the sheet and exposed [her] breasts, and started rubbing on [her] breasts," Farmer would later testify.
> #### "It didn't make sense to me that would happen. I so badly wanted to get off the table and the massage be done. I don't think there was any reason for her to be touching me that way." \- Annie Farmer
Jeffrey Epstein didn't participate in the massage, but Annie could feel his eyes close by.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b018c6c7-9cfb-442d-ad4d-b8ea8abde240?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Annie Farmer - GMA
In an interview later with Annie's mother, Janice Swain, the woman said she was told her daughter would be joined by "20 to 25 other students," but that when she came home she was "quiet and withdrawn."
When Maria Farmer discovered that her little sister had also been assaulted and tried to speak up, she received a phone call from Maxwell, threatening to burn all of her artwork.
In 2003 both of the Farmer sisters and their mother went to Vicky Ward of Vanity Fair--who was writing a expose on Jeffrey Epstein, the billionaire bachelor financier--to give a detailed report about their experience with Epstein and Maxwell. At the time, their names were nowhere on the record and this would be the first official accusation against the pair of sexual deviants. To put it lightly, the women were fearful. They knew both Epstein and Maxwell had bank accounts big enough to control politics, law enforcement, and the media. And they weren't wrong.
But Ward wrote the article, handing it to her boss, editor Graydon Carter, and departing to go on maternity leave. Later, she said she received calls from Epstein, asking her questions that made her "extremely uncomfortable," including where she would be giving birth. She said she found him threatening, especially after she began questioning his relationships with younger women. But eventually the article hit the fact-checking stage and Ward moved on. Then she received an email.
> #### "You're not going to believe this but Jeffrey Epstein is here. He's in the office. He's in Graydon Carter's office right now." \- Phone call from Vanity Fair fact-checker, recounted by Vicky Ward.
Ward said she was left out of the final decision-making.
> #### "I do not know what went on in that office. subject: The Mountain Minute: A Year in Review 🎊
body:
800 stories, 98 writers, 12.5M views — and the stories you refused to scroll past
| | | | [](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
---
**December 31, 2025** **A YEAR IN REVIEW**
| | Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family,
As we close out the final day of 2025, we wanted to pause — not to look ahead yet, but to look back. ___And if you'd rather listen to our year in review, you can listen[here](https://link.email.joinrmv.) or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.joinrmv.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.joinrmv.)!_
This year, Rocky Mountain Voice published more than **800 original stories** , written by **98 citizen journalists** across Colorado. That alone is something we’re proud of. But the real story isn’t the volume — it’s _why_ these stories mattered.
In 2025, our readers gravitated toward reporting that showed its work. You stayed with stories that pulled records, followed court filings, challenged redactions, and stuck with uncomfortable truths long after they stopped trending. You didn’t ask for hot takes — you asked for receipts.
Together, we: ✔ Tracked election integrity cases when others looked away ✔ Exposed failures in schools, courts, and regulatory agencies ✔ Amplified parents, whistleblowers, ranchers, students, and local officials ✔ Stayed with stories that affected real families, real livelihoods, and real communities
Across social media, more than **12.5 million people** saw RMV reporting this year. Nearly **1.6 million** **of you engaged** , shared, commented, and pushed these stories forward. In March, we launched the Mountain Minute Podcast which has already accumulated over **166,000 downloads**. And **46,000** patriots joined our community for the first time — not because we chased clicks, but because you recognized something different. _We'll be sharing our most viral social media moments for you tomorow!_
We’ve pulled together several end-of-year collections that reflect what you chose to read, share, and return to:
**📍[The RMV stories readers didn’t scroll past in 2025](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** **📍[The top 25 RMV team commentaries of 2025: Where we chose to stand](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** **📍[Voices from the Frontlines: Guest pieces that shaped the year](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** **📍[If 2025 had a playlist, these songs would be on it](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** **📍[Boots on the Ground, Uncovering Colorado’s Hidden Truths](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
These aren’t highlights curated by an algorithm. They’re a record shaped by reader attention.
Independent journalism doesn’t sustain itself by accident. It continues because people decide it matters — and because you chose to stay engaged when it would have been easier to scroll on.
Thank you for reading, sharing, challenging us, and standing with us this year.
We’ll see you in 2026.
— Team RMV
---
| | |
---

---

It took shape because readers kept stopping, reading, and sharing these guest commentaries. After the list, we step back and look at what that pattern tells us—and why it matters going into the new year._

It arrived unevenly. Some moments swallowed entire news cycles. Others barely registered at first, only making sense months later, once the consequences showed up. Most of the arguments about 2025 focused on motives or ideology. The consequences were easier to feel than to argue about._

You didn’t ask for hot takes — you asked for receipts. **Ask for Prayers and Hope for Blessings In The New Year**
For Immediate ReleaseDecember 31, 2025Contact: info@jeffwalterforcongress.com
Elburn, IL - Tuesday morning, December 30th, 2025, Elburn Mayor and Illinois 11th Congressional Candidate Jeff Walter received the heartbreaking news that his father, Winfried Hellmuth “Win” Walter, passed away early that morning. Jeff was very close with his father, and was lucky to have been able to spend the weekend with his family visiting his father, days before his passing. Win often remarked on how proud he was of his son, and his hope to be able to attend his son’s swearing in ceremony in Washington, DC if elected.
Jeff and his family are thankful for the outpouring of support from friends and neighbors during this difficult time. Jeff will return to the campaign trail soon, and thanks everyone for their understanding as he takes this time to be with his family. Memorial donations may be given to St. Francis de Sales High School or Notre Dame Academy, Toledo. Condolences can be shared at [www.sujkowski.com](https://jeffwalterforcongress.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cd07e5cbd6f962285e423156e&id=fd17179afc&e=fa724b03ca). For the full memorial write up, [https://www.sujkowski.com/obituary/Winfried-Walter](https://jeffwalterforcongress.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=cd07e5cbd6f962285e423156e&id=448539de5b&e=fa724b03ca).
Jeff, Carrie and their children wish everyone a Safe and Happy New Years Eve and New Years Day. As well as many Blessings For The Upcoming Year.

subject: This is the fastest way to get under my skin.
disclaimer_text: paid for by our campaign
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1001&akid=1491%2E251025%2ESTrQMy ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1002&akid=1491%2E251025%2ESTrQMy ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter, want to
know how to get under my skin?

Just say, “Abdul, we can’t win.”

People do say it straight to my face. Not voters, mind you. But pundits
and political consultants will say it to me all the time!

“You can’t win.”

Peter, can you
give me a chance to explain why they’re wrong? If I lay out the case, you
can decide for yourself. And if you’re convinced, I need your help. Deal?

Okay, so you hear the excuses people give...

— “Your name is Abdul – that’s too Muslim!”
— “AIPAC will spend millions against you!”
— “The Republicans will call you a commie!”
— “You’re too handsome and funny!”

Maybe not that last one. But you hear the others!

Let me break down why we don’t pay attention to the naysaying and why
we’re going to win this race in four key points:

- - -

1. General election polling says we can beat Mike Rogers.

A poll released just this month by Mitchell MIRS tested all of the
Democratic candidates. This wasn’t a poll paid for by our campaign. It was
an independent poll. And it says that we are statistically tied with Mike
Rogers. By the way, my primary opponent is not tied — and is actually
losing to Mike Rogers in this poll.

So we are tied in the polls with Mike Rogers before we’ve even had our
chance to mount our campaign. Before we ran a single ad or sent a mailer
or launched a big canvassing effort. I’d say that bodes pretty well.

2. The Democratic Primary is a three-way race, and we are rising to the
top.

I’m not a career politician or a state senator who's been in elected
office a long time. You might think a guy like me wouldn’t have a shot at
winning a contentious primary. But we started this primary with 24% of the
vote, in second place. And our AIPAC-backed opponent isn’t too far out of
reach. First place is within single digits, and we’re rising to the top.

3. We’ve earned tons of meaningful endorsements.

Bernie Sanders, Rashida Tlaib, Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Keith Ellison,
Andy Levin.

Michigan Democratic Party Progressive Caucus, Michigan Democratic Party
Grassroots Caucus, Michigan Democratic Party LGBT&A Caucus. Plus dozens of
county executives, city councilors, state representatives, and mayors.

I could list everyone here, but my email would be a bit too long!

4. We’re winning the fundraising battle.

This is critical because in 8-in-10 elections, the candidate who spends
the most money wins.

In the last quarter, we out-fundraised every single Democrat in this race
in terms of real contributions from real people. We did it even though I
have a hand tied behind my back. Because, unlike my opponents, I’ve never
once cashed a corporate PAC check and never will.

And by the way, this is thanks to YOU and your contributions.

- - -

Do you believe we can win now? Good. But, there’s a catch...

All our early momentum — the polls, the endorsements, the fundraising — is
great.

But if we don’t scale everything we are doing right now, we will fall
short on election day. We need more volunteers. More grassroots
fundraising. More people spreading the word.

I am betting that it’ll come. Because a lot of people are reading this
email just like you right now. And if even just 1-in-5 of us choose to get
involved, we would instantly make our campaign dramatically larger. We
would win this primary. Win the general. Then we go to the Senate and
fight like hell for money out of politics, money in your pocket, and
Medicare for All.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20251231-3-ak.S7v_X4&amount=10&refcode=em20251231-1491&t=1004&akid=1491%2E251025%2ESTrQMy ]So the catch is we can’t win without YOU. That’s why I have to ask...
will you make your
first $10 donation before tonight's
end-of-quarter deadline?

I’m calling it right now. If you and thousands of other people join
together to support this campaign right now, we are going to build a
movement the likes of which Michigan has never seen before. We are going
to defeat Mike Rogers and flip this state. And each one of us will have
one more vote and one loud voice in the U.S. Senate fighting for money out
of politics, money in your pockets, and Medicare for All.

But it starts with you taking a leap of faith to make
your first donation
to help us get there.

Yes, I believe that we will win.

Abdul

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20251231-3-ak.S7v_X4&amount=10&refcode=em20251231-1491&t=1023&akid=1491%2E251025%2ESTrQMy ]Donate $10 ››
